Start

What sharingu is, how to take it over and your first day.

What sharingu is

Source: docs/plan/README.md · What sharingu is

A closed loop for everything happening in an organisation. Contributions come from many kinds of people and from their AI tools; the MCP turns each one into structured records; the app shows them; people decide on them; what is still missing feeds the next contribution.

  • The MCP is the only input. Agents (and people, through their Claude or Codex) extract data from wherever it lives and FILE it through sharingu's MCP door.
  • sharingu holds its own truth, in D1. Goals, the aim, questions with their options and rulings, checks and their grades, cards, the model (screens, doors, tables, flows, gaps), the GTM template, docs — all in D1 tables inside the org's worker. No git "brain" repo is needed to run sharingu; the old brain repos are a one-time IMPORT SOURCE.
  • Everything is live. An MCP write shows on the app at once. Every tab reads D1. No publish step.
  • Versions are snapshots on demand (publish_version, restore_version).
  • One product; orgs and projects differ only by data. No per-org or per-project code. From sprint 6 one worker and one database serve every org (PLATFORM.md); until then the live org is ryuklabs, one worker of its own.
  • The three loops are the beta proof (the full gate is BETA.md):
  1. missing → file what it names → it shows, and the item closes;
  2. decisions → respond with an option → the question shows decided (owner) or answered (member) at once;
  3. a check → submit_grade with proof → the check shows graded on its goal and lights its map node.

Your first day

Source: docs/plan/HANDOFF.md · RESUME HERE; AGENTS.md · The commands

  1. Get the repo

    The engine's repo is private (ask the owner for access). Add the old repo as the read-only archive remote: the gate's history checks read old commits from it.

    git clone https://github.com/ryuk-labs/sharingu && cd sharingu
git remote add archive https://github.com/ryukdev/sharingu && git fetch archive
  2. Install

    Node and the engine's two dev dependencies (wrangler, esbuild).

    cd engine && npm ci
  3. Credentials

    The owner hands over the credentials file; it lives at ~/.sharingu/env-sharingu.sh (mode 600, three lines). Load it, never print a value. Nothing local needs it; live and the ship do.

    set -a; . ~/.sharingu/env-sharingu.sh; set +a
  4. Read the plan

    In this order: docs/plan/README.md → docs/plan/HANDOFF.md (the whole memory) → the current sprint in docs/plan/SPRINTS.md → AGENTS.md.

  5. Run it locally

    The local app with real data (it prints the URL), then the per-slice proof on a fresh worker. Nothing local reaches Cloudflare.

    sh tools/dev-local.sh up
sh tools/smoke.sh
  6. Validate live

    The ten-minute table below, with the credentials loaded. A red line: stop and tell the owner; never fix live by hand.

How we build

Source: AGENTS.md · How we build; Laws; docs/plan/HANDOFF.md · How builders are run; How the owner works

The process

  • One sprint, one branch. A sprint is a branch sprint-N off main in this checkout. No per-change worktrees, no per-change PRs, no verifier per change.
  • Vertical slices. A sprint is a list of slices in docs/plan/SPRINTS.md. A slice is built in this order: the table → the MCP/REST write → the screen that reads it. A slice is committed when its smoke is green.
  • Smoke per slice. sh engine/tools/smoke.sh boots the local worker, files through the MCP and loads the tabs. It is small and fast on purpose. The owner can open the local app after every slice.
  • Tests follow the code. When a slice replaces a page, the old checks that pinned that page's text are DELETED and replaced by smoke cases plus a selftest for any new logic. Never re-pin old text line by line.
  • One review at sprint end. The gate and the four suites run once (sh gate.sh, sh evals.sh, sh sims.sh, sh tools/tabs-verify.sh, sh tools/verify-live.sh in engine/; each suite starts a fresh local org, as the smoke does), one independent read-only review reads the whole sprint diff, the fixes land on the branch, then ONE PR is merged.
  • Ship after the merge, with the owner's OK, in the order sh tools/ship-plan.sh ryuklabs prints (from engine/): the budget, the migrations one at a time, the code with the import on the preview, then the walk on live.
  • Builders. The main session plans, briefs, reviews and commits. Opus sub-agents write a slice's code from a brief. Builders run one at a time when they share files (src/index.js, src/mcp.js); in parallel only on disjoint files.
  • Forks go to the owner as MCQs, recommended option first.
  • Update docs/plan/HANDOFF.md at every stop and tick docs/plan/SPRINTS.md. That is the only status ceremony.

The laws

  • The MCP is the only input; D1 is the truth; every screen reads D1 live. No page reads a published file.
  • One product; orgs and projects differ only by data. No per-org or per-project code (docs/plan/PLATFORM.md).
  • Secrets stay machine-local. Never print a value, never commit one. Credentials: set -a; . ~/.sharingu/env-sharingu.sh; set +a.
  • The ryuklabs account is on Workers Paid since 2026-10-02 (owner): D1 allows 25 billion rows read and 50 million written a month, with no daily limit, and a request gets real CPU time. The per-screen row budget below STAYS, because an outside team installs sharingu on its own account, which may be free.
  • Local first, and inside the Cloudflare FREE tier for any org that is not ours. A free account's daily limits are 5,000,000 D1 rows read, 100,000 rows written and 100,000 requests, shared by everything on it; a request also gets about 10 ms of CPU and 50 subrequests. Develop and test on the local worker. After each slice run node tools/page-budget.mjs against the local app with real data: a screen or MCP read over 1,500 rows is flagged and must be justified or cut (aggregate in SQL, never read a whole table to count it). The local worker does NOT enforce the CPU or subrequest limits, so the first live import and the first live load of each heavy page are checked by hand at ship, small batch first.
  • The Mini is shared. One heavy suite at a time; check uptime before a full suite.
  • A claim carries its proof: the command, its exit code, its output.
  • No dead code, no dead docs (owner, 2026-10-02): a doc names only what exists (tools/check-docs.py is a gate step).
  • Rules live in this repo, not in a session's memory and not on a board.

How builders are run

  • Opus sub-agents. One on the door files; others only on disjoint files, each from a frozen copy of the code when it needs a running worker. A brief names: what to read, the rulings it implements, what to build, the files it owns and must not touch, its ports, the non-negotiables (no widening of authority, nothing per org or project, the row budget, every statement through the scoped data layer), the tests that follow the code, the proof commands, how it must look at its own work, what to report. Builders never commit.
  • An auth change gets an independent, read-only adversarial review before its PR (sprint 21's fixes: two reviews, every finding folded).
  • Integrating a builder's work (from engine/): node --check every src/.js src/knowledge/.js · python3 tools/make-door-contract.py · python3 check-mcp-parity.py · python3 check-brand.py · python3 tools/code-atlas.py > code-atlas.json · python3 tools/check-boot-schema.py · python3 tools/check-docs.py · node tools/make-arch-client.mjs --check · node tools/copy-check.mjs --check · every tools/selftest.mjs the change touches · sh tools/smoke.sh (load under 8) · read the authority-relevant diff and the shots · commit only that builder's files · sh gate.sh (its contract-drift check reads what is COMMITTED) · the shots to the owner.
  • A builder's "green" is a claim; a screenshot is not a signed-in user (shots.mjs --cookie); rows written are counted, never estimated.

Rules that remove ambiguity: a fork that is not the owner's is decided by the plan's laws (one product, nothing per org or project, no widening of authority, the per-screen row budget) and recorded in SPRINTS.md; a builder cut off resumes from its engine/.runs/<name>/PROGRESS.md; a migration takes the next free number at integration time; no full suite outside a sprint end; load over 8 means wait, never skip the check.

How the owner works

  • Decisions go to the owner as MCQs, with an inline drawing first, the recommended option first, each with its cost. They decide fast, often correct the recommendation, and are usually right. They dislike bulk: keep prose tight.
  • They want to SEE the work: shots after every slice, and they judge the product by how it looks (LOOK.md).
  • Ask only for what is theirs (a ship or anything live, money, access design, scope they ruled on, anything irreversible); fold everything else into the plan and carry on.
  • A ship needs their OK each time. Never print a secret.
  • They may switch Claude accounts mid-work: keep this file current at every stop so the next session resumes cold.

Product

What the product does: the loops, the tabs, the join and the door.

The three loops

Source: docs/plan/README.md · What sharingu is; docs/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md · §5 The three loops

  • The three loops are the beta proof (the full gate is BETA.md):
  1. missing → file what it names → it shows, and the item closes;
  2. decisions → respond with an option → the question shows decided (owner) or answered (member) at once;
  3. a check → submit_grade with proof → the check shows graded on its goal and lights its map node.
  1. What is missing → file → it shows. missing reads the checklist (src/checklist.js over k_fill): the aim, the goal tree, options and rulings owed, gaps, a start-here doc, the model, checks and grades, the GTM template. Each open item names the preview call that fills it. Filing it closes the item on the next read — no publish.
  2. Decisions → respond → it shows. Decisions reads k_questions + k_options + the ledger overlay. The owner's non-provisional answer rules it at once; a member's answer shows as "answered, with the owner" and the owner rules it. Agents ask the owner a real, optioned question by filing a question.
  3. Checks → grade → it shows. k_checks is the register; check_results holds grades. Goals shows each goal's checks (via refs); the Map lights a node from its checks' latest grades (green all pass · red a fail · amber partly graded · grey none), and marks it stale when the node changed after the grade.

Roles and hats

Source: docs/plan/LOOK.md · Ruled by the owner (evening); Hats, archive and Broadcast

  • Roles: Admin · Member · Partner (an outside collaborator who sees only the projects they are seated on). A typed role label becomes a person's HAT on their profile.
  • Profile: name, photo or initials, title, one or more of the six website hats (Management · Engineering · Organization · Go-to-market · Finance · Partner); Home leads with what the hat needs; briefings follow the hat. A seventh, Quality (the testers: test runs, grades on checks, bugs found, release readiness), the owner's MCQ of 2026-10-10 (engine/src/hats.js).
  • Starter Broadcast: the web-and-mobile app pack — six agents (product spec, UX design, frontend, backend and API, QA verify, release), three workflows (build a web app, build a mobile app, fix a bug), three skills (file a contribution, grade a check, ask the owner).
  • Connect your AI shows setup for Claude (Code, Desktop, the claude.ai connector), ChatGPT and Codex.
  • All projects filled: siru, saruspay and bunny are imported from what is on this machine, so the UI is judged on real data across every project.
  • The ADMIN sets the hats that unlock briefings and cards (access_hats); a person's own hats shape only what Home shows first. The project archive / reactivate stays on Control.
  • Broadcast's live picture: the last week's contributions as dots flowing from people to the goals they name, replayed on open and live after; hover follows one person or goal; a dot opens its filing.
  • The starter pack is BUILT INTO the product (versioned with the engine, the same shelf for every org); Equip copies an item into the project.

The MCP door

Source: docs/plan/MCP.md · §0, §2, §5; contracts/door.json · the counts

37tools
19write tools
109REST routes
162error codes

0. Ruled by the owner (MCQ, 2026-10-01)

  • The person's AI client reads the input where it lives and extracts; sharingu runs no model.
  • The admin's agent creates a project through the MCP.
  • "Filled" is a full checklist per page, with a fill meter.
  • A light goes STALE when what it proves changes after the grade (a new picture of a screen does not: 2026-10-02).
  • Every filing is previewed first — always. The preview shows what will be filed, where it will show, how it will be graded and what it reaches.
  • The preview and the receipt are a card in the chat where the client can draw one, the same page in the app, and an inline text render for CLI users.
  • The plan is validated on our own scattered data, across every project we hold.

2. The door today: 37 tools, 90 REST rows (58 GET, 32 POST), 147 error codes

The tools are §5's. For an owner, the tools/list answer is 49,949 bytes of compact JSON (measured 2026-10-13 on a local worker, sprint 19's split; every tool's schema carries orgSlug since sprint 7). GET /capabilities serves the inventory generated from the contract: every tool and route, read or write, who may call it, and whether you may. POST /rank and POST /round are REST only, for Build's Rank button and Decisions' Add to round.

Regrade (sprint 4, R1): regrade {flow | node | checks} observes each stale or ungraded check's own page as the caller (one GET each, at most 8 a call) and files what came back as its grade; a walk, a check of another kind or an id it cannot fill comes back under needsProof with its preview call. Its REST twin, POST /regrade, is the Regrade press on a flow's view, a Map node and the Impact view: the first press shows the plan, the second files.

The words (owner, 2026-10-01): the thing people file is a CONTRIBUTION; the verb is "file". Also: a knowledge item, a check and its grade, a question and its ruling, a version, an open item. The engine's vocabulary check (tools/check-vocab-selftest.mjs) bans transmission, handoff, loop, heartbeat, capsule, holes and envelope on every face, the door's names and texts included.

Titles and annotations: every tool has a title and the four MCP annotations, set by one rule (read-only when it writes no row: 18 tools; open-world only wrap_up, which may open a GitHub issue); tools/annotations-selftest.mjs.

Every tool, route and error code: Build · The door's tools.

Its 19 skills

SkillWhat it does
ask-the-ownerPut a question to the owner the right way: a quick ask, or a decision with options on Decisions.
backend-apiModels the data and the doors, builds the API behind the screens, and files each change with its proof.
build-mobile-appFrom an idea to a mobile app in testers' hands and then in the stores, each step ending in a filed contribution.
build-web-appFrom an idea to a released web app in eight steps, each ending in a contribution the whole team can see.
draw-the-architectureRead the project's repo and draw its architecture: the parts, the services they run on, real journeys and the walls.
file-a-contributionRecord what you changed, decided or learned, aimed at the goal it moves, so the team sees it land.
file-the-screensRead an app's code and file its screens, the doors they call, the tables behind them and the checks each implies.
file-with-a-previewTurn anything you read into items, show the person exactly what will be filed and what it reaches, then file it.
fill-a-projectMake a new project and fill it from the person's own input, item by item, until its checklist has nothing open.
fill-the-gtm-sideTurn the person's mail, chats, meetings, CRM, revenue and search signals into GTM cards and contributions: summaries and links only.
fill-the-product-sideRead the code, docs, tickets and designs and file the product picture: goals, the Map's layers, decisions and docs.
fix-a-bugFrom a report to a proven fix in six steps: reproduce, pin it with a check, fix, prove, ship, close.
frontendBuilds the screens a person uses, against the map and its checks, and files each change with its proof.
grade-a-checkRun one check of the project's register exactly as written and grade it with proof.
product-specTurns an idea into the aim, goals, open decisions and checks a team can build against.
qa-verifyWrites the checks that prove the work, runs them, and grades each one with its proof.
releaseShips a version when its checks are green: confirms nothing blocks it, runs the release and files it with proof.
ux-designShapes the screens, flows and states a person moves through, and files them on the project's map.
weekly-reviewRead what changed across the org's projects this week, who filed what and with which AI, what waits on whom and what moved each goal.

What "clean like Obsidian and Claude Code" means here

  1. Quiet chrome. Navigation is a slim rail, not a bar of buttons. One accent (orange) used once per view; everything else is ink on paper. Each region of a page is its own card with a hairline edge; never a card inside a card.
  2. Type does the work. A clear scale (28 / 18 / 14 / 12), Manrope for people's words, mono for ids, counts and times. Numbers align. Nothing is ALL CAPS except the tiny mono labels.
  3. Dense but calm. Lists are rows with one line of meaning and one of context, 36–44px tall, generous left margin, no zebra, hover is a tint. A screen shows its most important thing first and never scrolls to reach it.
  4. Every state is designed. Empty, loading, unreachable and error are each a short phrase ("No goals yet") and at most one button — never a blank region, never a sentence of instructions, never a command on the screen.
  5. Fast and keyboard-first. No layout shift, no spinner for a read under 200 ms, a command palette for navigation and search, focus rings that are visible.
  6. Both worlds. Paper (light) and Ink (dark) from the same tokens, following the system setting.

Ruled by the owner (MCQ, 2026-09-30, after the sprint-1 ship)

  • Layout: a slim LEFT RAIL — the wordmark, the project switcher, the eight destinations, then the person, the theme switch and sign-out at the foot. Content takes the full height. Under ~860px the rail folds to a top bar with a menu.
  • Theme: follow the system — Paper in light, Ink in dark — with a manual switch that is remembered. Both from the SAME tokens.
  • Density: comfortable (rows ≈ 42px) on Home, Decisions, Goals, Build; compact (≈ 32px) only in the Map's inspector and long tables.

Added by the owner (2026-09-30, after seeing the foundation)

  1. The Map is the MAIN tab. It gets the highest quality in the product and is highly interactive (pan, zoom, layers, search, an inspector that feels instant, lights that change as checks are graded, flows you can follow).
  2. The sharingu logo is clean and universal: one part, the brand's approved vectors, the same everywhere (rail, phone bar, sign-in, public pages, empty states, errors, the favicon).
  3. Numbers, graphs and plots move: micro-interactions (a number counts up, a bar fills, a row responds) and macro ones (sections reveal, a changed metric pulses, a chart draws itself), to draw people in — one shared motion system, never per-page animation, off under reduced motion.
  4. Control shows how to connect: the MCP install and its config for each client, the versions, and the grading concept, explained on glass.
  5. Profiles: a person sets their own profile the way the website presents people — their hat (Management · Engineering · Organization · Go-to-market · Finance · Partner), and the app leads with what that hat needs.
  6. User management is simple, like Devin or Claude Enterprise: a members list, invite, role, remove.
  7. Broadcast is interactive, with a live picture of people contributing.
  8. sharingu ships with a starter Broadcast: simple agents and workflows to equip, following the standard approach to building a web or mobile app.

Ruled by the owner (MCQ, 2026-09-30, evening)

  • Roles: Admin · Member · Partner (an outside collaborator who sees only the projects they are seated on). A typed role label becomes a person's HAT on their profile.
  • Profile: name, photo or initials, title, one or more of the six website hats (Management · Engineering · Organization · Go-to-market · Finance · Partner); Home leads with what the hat needs; briefings follow the hat. A seventh, Quality (the testers: test runs, grades on checks, bugs found, release readiness), the owner's MCQ of 2026-10-10 (engine/src/hats.js).
  • Starter Broadcast: the web-and-mobile app pack — six agents (product spec, UX design, frontend, backend and API, QA verify, release), three workflows (build a web app, build a mobile app, fix a bug), three skills (file a contribution, grade a check, ask the owner).
  • Connect your AI shows setup for Claude (Code, Desktop, the claude.ai connector), ChatGPT and Codex.
  • All projects filled: siru, saruspay and bunny are imported from what is on this machine, so the UI is judged on real data across every project.

The Map, ruled (MCQ, 2026-09-30, night)

  • ONE canvas with layers (Screens · Doors · Data · Flows · Deps), Arch and the MCP tool list as views in the same toolbar; the seven pages fold into it.
  • A LAYERED layout: surfaces → screens → doors → tables in columns, curved links, stable positions.
  • All four interactions in the first version: hover highlights links and click pins the inspector · play a flow · live lights when a check is graded · minimap, fit, zoom and keyboard moves.
  • Node lights come from a maintained table; a load reads under 1,500 rows.
  • Owner, on the mockup: the toolbar and the side panel type were too big — a compact strip (12px pills, 11px mono) and a compact inspector (13/12/11px, ≤ 300px wide, truncation not wrapping). It must generalise to large projects (siru ~550 nodes, saruspay ~440 nodes / 3,850 checks): level of detail by zoom (dots without labels when zoomed out), collapsible clusters, find as the primary way in, dimming rather than hiding, and proven on saruspay and siru.

Hats, archive and Broadcast, ruled (MCQ, 2026-10-01)

  • The ADMIN sets the hats that unlock briefings and cards (access_hats); a person's own hats shape only what Home shows first. The project archive / reactivate stays on Control.
  • Broadcast's live picture: the last week's contributions as dots flowing from people to the goals they name, replayed on open and live after; hover follows one person or goal; a dot opens its filing.
  • The starter pack is BUILT INTO the product (versioned with the engine, the same shelf for every org); Equip copies an item into the project.

The screens atlas, ruled (owner, 2026-10-01)

"Wireframe and screen should be super cool as well: full screenshots and full wireframes of the various apps inside the project." The reference is Revyl's Atlas (https://x.com/tryrevyl/status/2103335699969941604); the owner's own example of the content is ~/Desktop/SarusPay Board.html.

  • A Screens view on the Map, per app inside the project: each screen as its real render, else its wireframe, else an outline (the person can switch), transitions as the nav edges, states as variants; pan and zoom like the Map; a click opens the screen's inspector.
  • Efficient in size and render; filed through the MCP in any form (html, image, wireframe), piece by piece, in ONE standard format; the core is never customised per project (ARCHITECTURE.md §11).

The revision (owner, 2026-10-02)

The whole front end is revised before the second video, on shared parts, in the brand above. No change to the MCP, the write door or the tables: the pages read what they read today.

  • Three depths on every page. Glance: one strip that answers "how is it going" with a number and a shape. Scan: one line per row (a title, one status, one number), grouped, with what is settled folded to a single line. Expand: the details open in place when asked for.
  • Clear segregation. A page is a few cards; each has a tiny mono label and one job.
  • People have faces. An avatar (the person's picture, else their initials) on every row a person owns, and a stacked row for who contributed.
  • Shapes over sentences. A segmented bar for done, in progress and not started; a bar per lane or area; a sparkline or small bar chart for a week; a ring for a count of a target. Drawn by the page as inline SVG, no chart library. Bars are ink; the status colours (green, amber, red) mean status only; orange stays once per view.
  • One filter row, the same on every list: status, area or lane, person, time, each chip with its count, the choice kept in the address.
  • Show the answer, not the label: a ruled question shows its ruling in one phrase; ids and refs live in the expanded row.
  • Pristine copy — no hints, no explanations on the screen. A screen holds titles, labels, values, names and buttons. It holds no helper paragraph, no "how this works", no legend that explains the product, no sentence telling the reader what their Claude could file, no raw call or JSON, no rule spelled out in prose, no "0 of something" that says nothing. What a control means lives in its title (a hover) and in the docs; what to file next lives on What is missing, as a list of items, each with a copy button. An empty region is a short phrase and at most one button.
  • Done when: every page in both worlds, at 1440 and 390, has been read by the main session and the owner, and the copy check (a selftest that reads every renderer's text) finds no sentence outside a title, a value or a person's own words.

The parts live in engine/src/parts.js (one stylesheet, PARTS_CSS, on the shell's tokens) beside ui.js; the gallery is node tools/parts-gallery.mjs (eight mock pages, shot in both worlds at 1440 and 390). The rail's current tab is a view's one orange; the parts use none. The copy check is tools/copy-check.mjs; its allowlist is empty and stays empty. The owner approved the gallery as shown (MCQ, 2026-10-02), with one new read (contributions per day and person for the last 7 days) and initials for faces (a person's own picture comes later: PLATFORM.md §4, after the road).

Order: the parts and their gallery (approved) → Home, Goals, Decisions, Build, GTM → the detail pages (a goal, a question, a contribution and its Impact, a card, a doc, a preview, the Library, What changed, What is missing, Broadcast, Control, Profile, Versions, Activity) → the Map's views get the copy rule only.

Rules for every screen change

  • Shared parts and tokens only: the parts in engine/src/ui.js and its one stylesheet; the tokens in engine/src/shell.js.
  • engine/tools/shots.mjs shoots the local app in both worlds at 1440 and 390 wide (--cookie as a signed-in user); the builder LOOKS at every shot, and the owner gets them.
  • The semantic hooks stay: every data-region, data-button, data-door, data-state attribute and every route keeps its name, so the smoke and the suites keep proving behaviour while the markup around them changes. A check that pins old class names or old copy is deleted, not re-pinned.

Build

How it is built: the architecture, the code, the data model and the whole door.

Architecture

Source: docs/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md · whole

The owner's model is in README.md. This file says HOW it is built TODAY: ONE worker and ONE D1 database serve many orgs, ryuklabs org 1, each org at its own address; what happens in an org stays in the org (§10, with the accounts, the sign-up and the address). Where each screen reads and renders is INVENTORY.md; the slices are SPRINTS.md.

1. The shape, in one picture

        agents / people (their Claude)                       the browser (8 tabs)
                  │  the one /mcp (OAuth or key)                      │  session cookie, /<org>/…
                  ▼                                                   ▼
   ┌──────────── the door: ONE worker, every org (ryuklabs-agent-r) ────────────────┐
   │  auth (accounts · seats · tokens · keys · OAuth) → the org → project → handler │
   │                                                                                │
   │  WRITE                                    READ                                 │
   │  preview → file    ─┐                ┌─ read tools + REST twins + pages         │
   │  (the write doors) ─┤─► D1 ◄─────────┤   (all live, same read per screen)      │
   │  human verbs       ─┘   │            └─ versions (snapshots in D1)              │
   │                         └─► cron, per org: reports, backup, prune (no webhooks)│
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        R2 keeps BLOBS (o<org>/…): saved files, wrap-up reports, backups, render bodies
  • D1 is the truth for every project's knowledge AND its ledger, every org's in the one database.
  • R2 holds no served truth. The worker reads nothing under R2 serve/; it reads R2 only for blobs (a saved file, a wrap-up report, a render body), each under its org's prefix (§10).
  • KV keeps only OAuth.

2. The data model (D1)

Every knowledge table carries project TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(key) and created_by / created_at / updated_by / updated_at. Primary keys are (project, id) unless noted. Ids are the caller's (validated), so an import is idempotent: an upsert by id. The validation rules live in ONE registry, src/knowledge/schema.js (KINDS), used by the write door, formats, the checklist, the preview and the importer.

TableHoldsKey fields
k_aimthe project's aim + measure (one row per project)aim (required), measure JSON {name,value,period,prior,priorPeriod,source} or a ruled absence, product_model (null, or none by design), source, as_of, confidence
k_goalsthe goal treeid, parent (one root; no cycles), title, dimensions ⊆ lane keys, weight, target, outcome_metric, owner, due, note, status, sort, source, as_of, confidence, budget (optional: allocated, spent, currency, source; rolled up the tree)
k_questionsquestions + their rulingqid, question, why, area, severity, status ∈ open·provisional·decided·superseded·moot, choice, label, rationale, decided_by, decided_at, affects, blocks, who_owes, waiting_on, impl_status, superseded_by, source. An open question has ≥2 options and no choice.
k_optionsa question's optionsPK (project, qid, idx), what, tradeoff
k_checkschecks (given/when/then)id, kind, method, severity, title, given, when_, then_, source_type, source_id, refs JSON (the node/goal/question ids it grades), rulings, status
check_resultsgradesone row per grade: check_id, status, graded_by, graded_at, the filing; the latest wins, the history stays
k_cardsany other knowledge cardPK (project, kind, id): name, status, body_md, role_visibility, as_of, confidence, source, refs (optional: the cards of the same project it relies on)
k_card_kindsthe kinds a project useskey, label, id_pattern, role_visibility, tab (the tab it lists on), review_after_days

| k_nodes | the MODEL: surface · lane · screen · door · table · entity · flow · gap · dep · evidence · service · architecture | type, id, name, status (live·planned·retired / open·closed), data JSON (type-specific) | A node's data may carry ownedBy (M3): the key of another active project of the org that owns the part, checked by name at the write door, never read across the fence.

k_edgesmodel relationsfrom_id, to_id, kind (nav · reads · writes · relation · depends · blocks · flow-step), label, data; PK (project, from_id, to_id, kind)
k_gtmthe GTM template (one row per project)template JSON (activityKinds non-empty), as_of, confidence
k_docsdocs, role briefs (capsules/<role>.md), start-here, the GTM strategy (gtm/…)path, title, body_md, role_visibility, as_of, confidence, source
k_versions · k_snapshotsthe version spine and a version's contentn, title, cause (published · restored), counts · PK (project, n, table_name, chunk), payload
k_renders · k_stylesa screen's frames and shared stylesheets (§11)the index only; bodies in R2

Kept by the write door and triggers, never written by a caller: k_check_refs and k_check_ungraded (which checks name a ref, which are ungraded), k_node_lights and k_node_links (a node's light and its edges), k_screen_renders, k_fill (the checklist's counts), k_node_stale and k_check_stale (stale proof, §12), and k_find (a contentless FTS5 index for search).

Platform-level (no org): accounts (one per email: the account passphrase's hash; migrate-070) and signup_codes (the operator's one-time codes, their hashes only; migrate-071). Org-level: people (a person's SEAT in one org, joined to its account by account_id), project_seats, projects, tokens (a session proven by the account's passphrase carries account_id, migrate-073), login_attempts. The ledger: transmission (a contribution: its shape, next action, pick-up and happened_at columns; transmission_refs and the tallies transmission_goals, transmission_kinds, transmission_open, each with an org-level bucket per org), events, loops (no project column), artifacts, approval_audit, check_results, previews (one row per preview). The nine org-wide tables (people, tokens, invites, events, artifacts, loops, approval_audit, login_attempts, transmission) carry an org column (migrate-067), and a trigger refuses a new row without one (migrate-068); projects.org and projects.slug are generated from the key (§10). The org table holds one row per org: name, slug (its address, unique, never a name the platform uses; migrate-072), brand, home, settings (migrate-063: domain, test seats, the repo a wrap-up's issue opens in, trace floor) and created_by_account (the account that created it through the door), read by src/tenant.js for the reader's org. Read by nothing: invites (the sign-up codes are signup_codes; it goes in a contract migration, PLATFORM.md §3).

Budget. Reads are bounded by indexes on (project, …), one statement per screen region (src/hotsql.js, pinned by tools/d1-hot-selftest.mjs); tools/page-budget.mjs flags a load over 1,500 rows read (in the shared database it keeps one org from blocking the rest; the budget stays at the free tier's scale: 5M rows read and 100k written a day).

3. The MCP door — writes

Every write is previewed, then filed by its own tool (sprint 19: OpenAI's scan asked that each write be its own tool). preview (and POST /preview) takes items in three forms — a contribution, a knowledge upsert, a knowledge remove — runs each through the same checks its write door runs, writes only its own row in previews, and answers for each item the tool that files it. file_contribution, save_knowledge and remove_knowledge (and POST /preview/file-contribution, /preview/save-knowledge, /preview/remove-knowledge) each take the preview's id and the same items of their part and file what is ready, through the write doors, in order (a grade goes through submit_grade, an answer through respond):

Write doorWhoDoes
knowledge items {kind, op, data}any seated member; role-limited kinds by rolevalidates each op with the registry, applies all in ONE DB.batch (all or nothing), files ONE ledger row (lane leader, kind knowledge). Kinds: aim · goal · question · check · card · card_kind · node · edge · gtm · doc · render · style. At most 200 ops a call; 256 KB of bodies.
contributions {contribution}seatedthe ledger; the shape checked; goalRef checked against k_goals; ids a contribution names checked against the project's own Map (src/maprefs.js)
grades {grade} (and submit_grade)seatedcheckId must exist in k_checks; proof is a stated result with its numbers, a command with its result, or a link
answers {answer} (and respond)seatedthe owner's non-provisional answer rules the question at once; a member's waits for the owner

Verbs beside them: rule_question and decide_contribution (owner), publish_version / restore_version (owner), create_project (admin), pick_up, publish and equip (refused to a Partner by role class), ask, save_file, open_items, wrap_up; REST only, POST /rank and POST /round. Every tool and REST row is declared in src/index.js (MCP_TOOLS, CAPABILITIES) and contracts/door.declared.json; contracts/door.json is generated.

Sign-in, one rule: a browser navigation without a session goes to sign-in; anything else is answered 401. An id door checks the caller before the lookup. The sign-in sets the request's org: the org of the seat the credential (a key, a session, an OAuth grant) found — under an org's address, a seat of that org only; for an account's grant, its seat in the org a call names (orgSlug) or its current one, never an org it holds no seat in. One request, one org (src/data.js).

4. Reads — one knowledge store, the project scope

  • src/knowledge/ — the readers every page uses: store.js (the generic readers behind read {kind}), and one module per shape: goals.js, decisions.js, canvas.js, checks.js, docs.js, cards.js, mapmodel.js, versions.js, screens.js, stale.js (stale by change), fresh.js (due by age). Per-request memo (reqmemo.js), one statement per shape.
  • Extract — src/extract.js: search, read, changes, brief, each one function behind its tool, its REST twin and its page (src/extractpage.js; a card's page src/cardpage.js). A card kind lists on the tab it names (src/tablists.js).
  • The project scope lives in src/project.js: a named project needs a seat (the owner: any active project of the org), else the caller's active project (a live stamp or the one seat), else the first project they may read in key order (§10). A write's stamp is doorProject's (src/core.js); INVENTORY.md §Scope lists the rest.
  • D1 only (owner, 2026-09-30): every tab and its read tools read D1, with no R2 fallback.

5. The three loops — how each closes

  1. What is missing → file → it shows. missing reads the checklist (src/checklist.js over k_fill): the aim, the goal tree, options and rulings owed, gaps, a start-here doc, the model, checks and grades, the GTM template. Each open item names the preview call that fills it. Filing it closes the item on the next read — no publish.
  2. Decisions → respond → it shows. Decisions reads k_questions + k_options + the ledger overlay. The owner's non-provisional answer rules it at once; a member's answer shows as "answered, with the owner" and the owner rules it. Agents ask the owner a real, optioned question by filing a question.
  3. Checks → grade → it shows. k_checks is the register; check_results holds grades. Goals shows each goal's checks (via refs); the Map lights a node from its checks' latest grades (green all pass · red a fail · amber partly graded · grey none), and marks it stale when the node changed after the grade.

6. The frontend (8 tabs — live data)

TabReads
Homethe aim and its measure · goals moved · what needs you · follow-ups due · what changed · the checklist's meter
Buildcontributions (knowledge writes too) · tempo · the finish line from k_goals
GTMthe template's lanes · the Strategy docs under gtm/ · the card kinds that name GTM · follow-ups due
Goalsthe goal tree + the ledger roll-up by the month the work happened + checks per goal
Decisionsk_questions/k_options + overlay; the question page; round
Mapone canvas with layers from k_nodes/k_edges, Arch, the Screens view (§11), lights and stale marks; Versions
Broadcastthe shelf, the built-in starter pack, the live picture
ControlMembers · Projects · Connect · Admin

Every tab carries its checklist chip and what changed since the project's version. Every empty state names the preview call that fills it (then the write tool the preview names). The look: LOOK.md.

7. Hooks — none outbound (owner, 2026-09-30)

The MCP is the intake; nothing outside needs sharingu to call it back, so there are NO outbound webhooks. What stays: the cron, once per org (the report backfill, the backup dump, the prune of expired previews), and the opt-in GitHub issue on a wrap-up.

8. The importer (use-and-throw)

  • engine/tools/import-brain.mjs <source> --project <key> [--layout kit|bank|pack|board|code] [--renders <file|dir>] [--overlay <ops.json> …] [--url <worker>] [--dry-run] reads one source (engine/tools/import/read*.mjs: a kit brain, a markdown knowledge bank, a served pack, a board directory, or this repo's code), maps each item to a knowledge op validated with the registry, folds in the overlays, and FILES them through the door in batches with a clientRef per batch, so a re-run is a no-op. It then reads every kind back: stored must equal built. It counts the rows each call writes and refuses a live run the account's plan cannot take.
  • engine/tools/dev-local.sh up imports every project into a local org; engine/tools/import-live.sh runs the same import against a version preview during a ship (SHIP_PREVIEW_HOOK), smallest project first, with an optional prune.
  • The sources and their order are in engine/tools/dev-local.sh: ryuklabs (the ops brain), sharingu (this repo's code, its wireframes from the old brain, its overlays), siru, saruspay, bunny, and demo (no source: the website's pitch as overlays).
  • sharingu's history (its contributions and screen pictures) is filed after the import by engine/tools/ship/after-import.mjs, through preview and the write tools.
  • An imported source is frozen (a read-only archive). The kit reader is engine/tools/import/load.mjs.

9. sharingu plans itself in sharingu

The sharingu project holds the product's model and checks generated from this repo's code, the owner's rulings, the goals and the docs from this plan (overlays under engine/tools/import/overlays/sharingu/), and its history as contributions. docs/plan/ stays the working plan across sessions.

10. The project and the org

The project a request reads is found once at the door (src/project.js resolveProject) and carried on the request; every reader asks projectOf(env). The org's facts are its D1 row (org, read by src/tenant.js for the reader's org): the MCP greeting and Map · Arch name the org from it. The worker reads nothing from R2 serve/.

The org wall. One database holds every org; what happens in an org stays in it:

  • The key carries the org. A project's key is o<org>--<slug> for every org but org 1, whose keys are its bare slugs (the live keys unchanged); the slug is unique inside its org and never holds --, and the org's number (not its name) rides the key, so renaming an org never rekeys (src/project.js orgOfKey; projects.org and projects.slug generated from the key). Everything kept apart by project is kept apart by org; a bare slug a caller types resolves inside the reader's org only.
  • One scoped data layer. Every statement runs on db(env) (src/data.js), which writes in the reader's org from the sign-in; a statement that names the org with no one signed in is refused, never run as org 1. The caches and request memos are keyed by org. The gate's tools/check-scoped-data.py fails a statement or an R2 key outside the layers.
  • An owner owns one org. The admin is the admin of its own org; storage, the log, the backup dump, the measures and clean-eval answer the reader's org alone. Work across orgs (allowing an email, one org's undo) runs only with the deployment's credentials, from the operator's machine, never through a seat.
  • An org is born one way: POST /orgs (src/orgs.js, the page /orgs/new): an account, proven by its own passphrase (never a seat's key), makes the org, its owner seat and its first project in one batch; one org per account (the beta's free tier). The platform is hosted-only (2026-10-09); a second platform the operator boots is this same code on another worker, booted empty (engine/ORG-SETUP.md).
  • Storage carries the org. Every R2 object lies at o<org>/<key> (src/storage.js, the one place keys are spelled); a file read by its exact id is looked up under its row's org. A bare key is no org's (org 1's were moved by tools/ship/r2-org-keys.mjs at the sprint-6 ship).
  • The cron runs per org (src/cron.js): each step once for each org, as the deployment for that org, at most 20 orgs a run; the nightly backup lands under the org's own prefix.
  • One org's undo. Time Travel restores the WHOLE database, so it is a platform incident tool. One org's undo is engine/tools/org-undo.mjs on the deployment's credentials: export the org, restore it under a new org id with every remap recorded, verify it table by table, delete one org (never org 1, never without a fresh matching export).
  • Proven in the gate. tools/attack-xorg.mjs holds two orgs, their data filed through the door, and, as each org's owner and member against the other, calls every tool, resource and route: no answer carries the other org's rows, none is a 5xx, the other org's tables stay unchanged. The one ruled exception: a public file read by its exact id answers from any org (ADR-055, kept while sign-up is allowlisted; PLATFORM.md §2.7). Contribution ids stay numbered across the database.
  • Accounts and seats, two secrets. One account per email (src/accounts.js), a seat per org it belongs to. The account's passphrase is its holder's alone (set by the sign-up, or proven on /profile) and signs in to every seat of the account; a seat's own key (its admin hands it over and rotates it) opens that seat alone, and never creates an org. The lockout counts per account; an attempt counts in the org of the seat the sign-in chose.
  • Joining (sprint 21): a new team requests access at /request-access (a profile and a passphrase, or Google), confirms its email, waits in line, and is approved by the operator, whose approval emails "You're in"; every email From hello@sharingu.xyz under the cap (src/email.js). Who holds an account is one rule (ACCOUNT_HELD), and a first passphrase set by a reset or Google makes the account's seats wait for its yes (engine/CLAUDE.md).
  • Sign-up by code (the operator's own path and the reviewer accounts'): only an email the operator allowed signs up, with the one-time code the operator hands over by hand (tools/operator.mjs, the deployment's credentials; single-use, expiring, revocable; no route mints one). The sign-up makes the account, or gives a passphrase-less account its passphrase.
  • The address (src/orgpath.js): every page of an org at /<slug>/…, the platform's own routes at the root (sign-in, sign-up, creating an org, the picker, /mcp, OAuth, health). Under an address only that org's people sign in (a bearer of its org, a browser session as its seat there); an unknown org, a platform path under an org and a credential with no seat there answer one 404. A cookie at the root signs no one in (a page navigation goes to the session's org). One URL helper builds every link (tools/check-org-paths.py). A root page before sign-in wears sharingu's brand, an org's address its own; an account in several orgs picks one after sign-in, and the rail switches.
  • One /mcp, two grant kinds (src/oauthgrants.js): an OAuth grant signed in with the account's passphrase reaches the account's own seats, one org a call (orgSlug, else its current org); one signed in with a seat's key reaches that seat forever. A bearer key is its seat. Any other org is org_unreachable before a call runs, the same answer whether the org exists or not; whoami lists the orgs a connection reaches.

11. Screens and renders — the standard (owner, 2026-10-01)

The owner's rule: sharingu is a tool, like Claude Code — the core never changes per project. A project's screens reach the app the way everything else does: an agent files them through the MCP in ONE standard format, appends and updates piece by piece, and the Screens view shows them. Importers and per-source mappers are TOOLS outside the core.

  • A screen is a node of type screen: data.surface (the app or apps it belongs to), data.lane and data.step (where it sits in its app's flow; optional — the layout falls back to the nav edges), data.states, data.wireframe (optional).
  • A render is the kind render: { screen, state?, variant?, format: "html" | "image" | "wireframe", body | artifact, style?, width?, height? }, keyed by (project, screen, state, variant). html is a fragment (no script runs: stored stripped and shown sandboxed); image is a png, jpeg or webp sent as base64 in body, or a banked artifact the writer filed themselves or a public one (an SVG is refused: it can carry a working link); wireframe is the grammar as JSON. An upsert replaces that one render; an unchanged body (same hash) writes nothing. Every take is kept (k_screen_takes, migrate-065: one row per filing of a frame, the body by its hash): a screen's inspector shows its previous takes, and a previous take is restored through the door as the person (a render upsert naming the hash with no body; POST /render/restore is the page's press). A new picture never makes a grade stale (owner, 2026-10-02).
  • A style is the kind style: { id, css } — a stylesheet many html renders share.
  • Storage: the BODY goes to R2, content-addressed (o<org>/renders/<project>/<sha256>), immutable and cacheable; D1 keeps only the index (k_renders). The Screens view reads the index in one statement and loads bodies lazily.
  • The wireframe grammar (src/wireframe.js, drawn by the engine as SVG): a list of blocks — header · nav · tabbar · title · text · input · button · list · card · image · divider · spacer — each with an optional label, lines/items count and emphasis.
  • Limits: an html body ≤ 200 KB, a wireframe ≤ 50 KB, a picture ≤ 1 MB, a style ≤ 200 KB; a call carries ≤ 256 KB of bodies and names ≤ 1 MB of banked pictures; the door says which op was over.

12. Filling a project, and impact (owner, 2026-10-01)

The loop the product closes: fill → change → impact → re-prove.

  • Who does what. The person's own AI client reads the input where it lives and extracts on the person's machine and plan. sharingu runs NO model: it validates against the standard, stores, shows, and answers what is still missing. The credential picks the person (role and seats) and, with them, the org (an account's grant: the org a call names); project picks the project.
  • The checklist is the standard. One list in the core (src/checklist.js), the same for every project, counted only in the areas a project has. Every item is a bounded aggregate over k_fill and carries the call that fills it. missing is its reader; the meter is its count. A project never gets its own list.
  • The fill kit. create_project (admin only), formats (generated from the registry), and the built-in "Fill a project" skill. Everything works through tools alone. Bulk input goes through the same door in batches from a script the agent writes; the importers under engine/tools/import/ are one such script.
  • Impact. A change is a contribution (it names what it touches) or a knowledge write. Its reach (src/reach.js, src/impact.js) is a bounded walk over what D1 holds: k_node_links, k_check_refs, the goals of those checks, the questions that name the node. Computed on read, never stored, never a table scan.
  • Stale proof. A check graded before its node last changed is stale: the light shows it and missing asks for the regrade. Three trigger-kept rows (k_node_stale, k_check_stale, the k_fill row stale); a change counts only on a graded node.

Scope — one rule, plus the write stamp and the raw session stamp

  • src/project.js — THE rule for a read: a named project (a tool argument, ?project= on a GET twin or on a brain:// URI; a bare slug resolves inside the reader's org) needs a seat (the owner: any active project of the org), else the caller's active project (a live stamp or the one seat), else the first project they may read in key order. resolveProject finds it once at the door (the router, callTool, resources/read) and carries it on the request's env; every reader asks projectOf(env). A non-owner seated nowhere reads the org-level rows in an org of several projects, the one project in an org of one, and a Partner reads no project in any org (NO_PROJECT, the fence).
  • doorProject (src/core.js) — the write stamp: a named project checked against the seats (the owner: any active one), else a single seat, else the live stamp, else the org's one active project (never for a Partner with no seat: refused, and an org-level record such as ask lands at the org level); anything else is refused project_forbidden or project_required.
  • tokenProjectFor (src/core.js) — the raw session stamp (tokens.project, set by POST /project), read by the file list (read_file with no id, GET /artifacts). The owner's "All projects" pick writes '*' into that column, which references projects(key).

Not project-scoped at all: a person's open items (open_items; the loops table has no project column).

Known faults

  • None open. (A wrap_up's answers matching only the old questionnaire's ids was fixed by sprint 5 W1.)

Auth (keep)

A key is TOKEN_PREFIX + hex(20), stored as people.key_hash (sha256) and pass_hash (pbkdf2); the key IS the seat's passphrase. One ACCOUNT per email (accounts, src/accounts.js): sign-in finds the account by its email, then its seat in the org the address serves; the password is the account's passphrase (set only by its holder — on /profile by proving it, or by the one-time-code sign-up) or that seat's own secret (an admin's to set, opening that seat alone). Signing in mints a 90-day session token, stored as a sha256 in tokens, carried in the __Host-ar_session cookie; LOGIN_SESSION_SQL (src/accounts.js) inserts it only if the verified secrets are unchanged. A read-only credential is derived from the key (READ_ONLY_SUFFIX, src/core.js); a key in ?k= reads and never writes; cookie writes are same-origin checked (csrfRefused); sign-in locks after 8 failures in 15 minutes (src/accounts.js LOCKOUT_FAILS, lockOf; the same lock on sign-up, creating an org and /profile), keyed by the ACCOUNT and the CLIENT (login_attempts.client, migrate-077: clientOf, the caller's address): a client the account's own passphrase signed in from in the last 30 days is judged by its own failures, every other vantage (a seat secret's, no client) by the account's failures from everywhere — so a stranger knowing only the email never locks the holder's own client; plus the LOGIN_LIMIT binding (shared by sign-up and creating an org). At the root the sign-in NEVER defaults an org: a seat-key sign-in and a one-org account go straight in; a several-org account picks at the picker (GET /orgs, src/orgpicker.js); a JSON sign-in answers 409 choose_org and names its org — as does an account's passphrase while any seat of it waits for its holder's yes (its JSON sign-up then signs in nothing: the owner's ruling, 2026-10-09); the OAuth form asks a several-org account the same choice (src/oauth.js, src/login.js). A session proven by the account's passphrase reads as the account's seat under any of its orgs' addresses, a session proven by a seat's key stays that seat's (tokens.account_id). A seat an admin adds for an email whose account already holds a passphrase or a seat in another org is PENDING (people.pending, migrate-074): inert — its key answers 401 — until its holder accepts or declines it on the picker (POST /orgs/seat); the admin's flash says the seat waits, and remove-person withdraws it. ONE revocation rule: the holder's own passphrase change ends every other session of the account; an admin's seat action ends only that seat's seat sessions and seat grants (src/secrets.js, src/oauthgrants.js {seatOnly}), and an admin's reissue (rotate-key, set-password) bumps the seat's grants epoch (people.reissued_at): an account grant made before it stops acting in THAT seat until its holder connects again (accountGrantStands). add-person and sign-up refuse a non-ASCII email (email_not_ascii, src/accounts.js asciiEmail). CREATING AN ORG (src/orgs.js, GET /orgs/new, POST /orgs): proven by the ACCOUNT's passphrase only, one org per account, its address never a reserved name (src/orgnames.js, derived from the routes; tools/check-org-names.mjs is a gate step); the owner key is shown once. JOINING (sprint 21, src/requestaccess.js, src/accounts.js): the way in for a new team is /request-access (a profile and a passphrase, or Google) → the emailed check → the line → the operator's approval (operator.mjs allow --request, or the operator page) and its "You're in" → sign in → /orgs/new; an email whose account is held (ACCOUNT_HELD) gets "you already have an account" instead. SIGN-UP BY CODE (src/signup.js, GET/POST /signup, the operator's own path and the reviewer accounts'): only an email the OPERATOR allowed, with the one-time code the operator hands over by hand (tools/operator.mjs allow, on the deployment's credentials — no app seat mints one; only the code's sha256 is stored, signup_codes; single-use, expiring, revocable); it creates the account, gives a passphrase-less account its passphrase, or — the operator's --reset — replaces one and ends every session of every seat; every refusal is one answer (invalid_signup) and counts in the account's lockout, and a valid code passes the lock (the operator's code is possession proof); an account passphrase is at least 12 characters, a seat's own secret at least 4. A browser navigation without a session goes to sign-in; anything else is 401. The sign-in sets the request's org: the org of the people row the credential found (src/data.js signIn); one request, one org. OAuth for MCP clients keeps its grants in KV OAUTH_KV, keyed by person, scopes mcp:read and mcp:write; a grant is an ACCOUNT's (its own seats, one org a call: orgSlug) or a SEAT's (src/oauthgrants.js), and a grant with no credential stamp answers 401. The admin is people.role = 'owner' of its own org; an org never has zero admins. A public file read by its exact id answers from any org (ADR-055, ruled kept while sign-up is allowlisted, PLATFORM.md §2.7); every list stays inside the org.

Hooks

Crons 0 3 and 0 15 (wrangler.jsonc) → src/cron.js, each step once per org (at most 20 orgs a run): the reports backfill, the backup dump of the org to R2 o<org>/backups/d1/ (src/backup.js: every table boot.sql creates is dumped, rebuilt on restore, or never dumped with its reason; people without credentials) and the prune of expired previews. R2 otherwise holds only blobs, every key under its org's o<org>/ (src/storage.js): saved files under inbox/artifacts/, wrap-up reports under inbox/handoffs/ and the render bodies renders/<project>/<sha256>. Outbound: the GitHub issue a wrap_up may open (src/handoff.js, only when GH_TOKEN, one for the whole worker, is set and the org row's settings name a handoffRepo). Inbound webhooks: none.

Failure classes and error codes

Source: contracts/door.json · inventory.failures; errors

ClassMeaningNext action
not-authenticatedNo valid credential reached this door — no session cookie, and no valid Authorization: Bearer token resolved to a person (a key in the address signs no one in).Authenticate — sign in, send a valid bearer token, or a valid reader key — then retry the exact same call.
not-allowedThe caller authenticated fine, but its role, scope, or ownership may not do this specific thing (an owner-only door, a read-only OAuth grant on a write tool, a credential that doesn't own the resource).Do not retry unchanged — this is a role/scope/ownership gate, not a transient failure. Use a credential that holds the right role or scope, or ask its holder.
not-foundThe door authenticated the caller fine, but the id/ref/key asked for does not exist, or isn't visible to this caller.Check the id/ref for a typo or staleness; do not retry the exact same call unchanged.
162 codes
CodeClassMeaningNext actionFiles
account_existsPOST /request-access with google=1 (sprint 21, 21.4c) for an email an account holds by now (or a Google account another account is linked to): nothing was filed. HTTP 409.Sign in instead: Continue with Google (GET /auth/google/start?intent=signin) or POST /login with the account's passphrase.index.js
account_standsPOST /signup with an org's invite link (sprint 12, 12.3): the invited email's account already stands — it holds its own passphrase, or a seat in another org — so the link sets no passphrase and changed nothing (no passphrase, no seat, the link not spent).Sign in at /login with your account passphrase; if the seat waits for your yes, accept it on your org list (GET /orgs). An account with no passphrase yet gets one by the operator's sign-up code (POST /signup).invite.js
already_currentnot-foundPOST /versions/restore (restore_version) named the current version and nothing was filed since it, so there is nothing to restore; or POST /broadcast/equip named the version a project is already on (its newest equip of that slug). Nothing was filed.Do not retry unchanged: pick an older version from GET /versions (the versions tool) to restore, or another version of the item (GET /broadcast lists the shelf and where this project stands) to equip.broadcast.js knowledge/versions.js
already_decidedThis contribution already carries a terminal decision (approve/reject/needs-work) — decide_contribution and POST /contribution/:id/decide close on the first decide and refuse a second (closed-loop idempotency guard, ADR-072).Do not retry — read the row back (read / GET /contribution/:id) to see the decision that already landed.core.js
already_publishedPOST /broadcast/publish named a draft that is published already (each draft is one version). Nothing was filed.Do not retry: file a new draft of the same slug for its next version, then publish that one.broadcast.js
already_seatedPOST /orgs/seat accept (sprint 7's review, A1): your account already holds an active seat in that org (one account, one seat per org), so the waiting seat cannot become a second. HTTP 409; nothing changed.Use the seat you hold there; ask that org's admin to withdraw the duplicate invitation.accounts.js
auth_requirednot-authenticatedNo reader resolved from this request — no session cookie, and no valid Authorization: Bearer token (a key in the address signs no one in).Authenticate and retry the exact same call.index.js knowledge/screens.js mapnode.js mapplanes.js util.js
bad_answernot-foundA JSON-RPC response POSTed to /mcp (a client's answer to a confirm, sprint 3 D3) was neither an elicitation result (action accept, decline or cancel) nor a JSON-RPC error. bad_beforechanges {org: true, list: true} was sent a before that is not a cursor this read gave. Nothing was read.Send the previous answer's next exactly as it came, or leave before out for the newest page.activity.js
bad_consentThe consent grade sent to /profile isn't one of the allowed values (see the accompanying `allowed` list).Retry with one of the allowed grades.index.js
bad_cursorPOST /backup-dump?page=<cursor> was sent a cursor no page answered (the dump's pages are walked from "" by each answer's next). Nothing was read.Start again with page= (empty), and send each answer's next as the following page; next null ends the dump.backup.js
bad_emailPOST /account/resend or POST /account/forgot whose email is not one plain ASCII address (sprint 21, 21.4a). Checked before anything is read: it says nothing about which emails hold an account.Send {email} as one plain address.index.js
bad_fieldA knowledge item sent a field whose value breaks its kind's rule: the wrong type, a value outside its list, a measure, template or options list in the wrong shape, a required field sent empty, a goal naming itself as parent, a node status its type does not take. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops). Or (sprint 3, B1) a contribution's shape field broke its rule (preview, POST /preview): `field` names it (next.by, source[3].kind, depends[0]), with a `hint` and an `example`; nothing was filed.Send the field as the error's note says, then the whole batch again.knowledge/schema.js knowledge/screens.js knowledge/write.js preview.js render.js shapes.js
bad_hatPOST /profile set-profile named a hat that is not one of the seven (management · engineering · organization · gtm · finance · partner · quality). Nothing was saved.Retry with hats from the accompanying `allowed` list (an empty list clears your hats).index.js
bad_idA knowledge item's key field is missing or malformed (a goal id is a lowercase slug, a qid matches the engine's QID rule, other ids carry no spaces, comma or |, an edge kind is one of the listed ones). Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Send the key as the note says, then the whole batch again.knowledge/schema.js
bad_invitePOST /signup with an org's invite link (sprint 12, 12.3): a field is missing or malformed, checked before anything is read (`field`: invite · passphrase · confirm, with a `note`): the invite is the link's 48-character token (the whole link is taken too), the passphrase at least 12 characters.Open the invite link again (or paste it whole), and choose a passphrase of at least 12 characters, the same one twice.invite.js
bad_laneThe lane named isn't one of the org's TX_LANES (see `allowed`).Retry with one of the allowed lanes.activity.js core.js
bad_opA knowledge item is not {kind, op: "upsert" | "remove", data: {…}}. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Send each op in that shape, then the whole batch again.knowledge/schema.js preview.js
bad_orgPOST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): a field is missing or malformed, checked before anything is read (`field`: email · password · name · slug · project · you, with a `note`): the slug (the org's address) takes a-z, 0-9 and single dashes, 2 to 40 characters, never opening or closing on a dash; the first project's slug 2 to 30 the same way. It says nothing about accounts or about which addresses orgs hold.Fix the named field and send again.index.js orgs.js
bad_personchanges {org: true, list: true} was sent a person that is not a person's id. Nothing was read.Send an item's by.id (whoami answers your own), or leave person out.activity.js
bad_projectcreate_project was sent a key that is not 2 to 40 characters of a-z, 0-9 and dashes, or no name: nothing was created (the same rule POST /control add-project holds).Send key as a lowercase slug (e.g. "acme-web") and a name, then create_project again.admin.js mcp.js

Or `read` (GET /read) was sent a ref of no known form (goal/<id> · q/<qid> or question/<qid> · check/<id> · card/<kind>/<id> · doc/<path> · a node id · T-YYYYMMDD-NNN).Retry with a ref of one of those forms, or gap=1 to start the walk over the open gaps.extract.js mapnode.js
bad_request_accessPOST /request-access (sprint 21, 21.1): a field is missing or malformed, checked before anything is written (`field`: name · email · company · role · team_size · website · linkedin · x · github · ai_tools · use_case, with a `note`): name, a plain-ASCII work email, company, role and a team size of 1, 2-10, 11-50, 51-200 or 201+ are required; website an http(s) address (a bare domain is taken), linkedin, x and github that service's address or a handle. bad_sincechanges (GET /changes) was sent a since that is neither an ISO time nor a version (v4). Nothing was read.Retry with since: 2026-10-01, 2026-10-01T09:00:00Z or v4, or leave it out for the current version.activity.js extract.js
bad_srcGET /view's ?src= must be a same-origin path starting with an allowed prefix (see `note`) — refused before proxying anywhere (no open redirect).Retry with src set to one of the allowed prefixes.index.js
bad_statechanges {org: true, list: true} (GET /changes?org=1&list=1, GET /audit?all=1) was sent a state outside landed · with · decided · needs. Nothing was read.Retry with one of the states listed in `allowed`, or leave it out.activity.js
bad_verdictThe verdict sent isn't one of the allowed values for this door (decide_contribution: approve/reject/needs-work; submit_grade: proven/refused/incomplete — see `allowed`).Retry with one of the allowed verdicts.core.js knowledge/grades.js
batch_failedOne grade or answer of a call did not come back from the batch door, so it is not filed; the answer names it, the others stand.Send the same call again with the same clientRefs: what landed is found by its clientRef and never filed twice.knowledge/grades.js
blob_missingThe artifact's own database row exists, but the R2 object it points at is gone — a storage-layer inconsistency, not a caller mistake.Do not retry the same call — this needs an operator to check storage; report it.index.js knowledge/screens.js mcp.js
check_id_requiredsubmit_grade's call needs a `checkId` and none was sent.Retry with `checkId`.knowledge/grades.js
choose_orgPOST /login (JSON) with your ACCOUNT's passphrase (sprint 7's review, A1): your account holds seats in several orgs, or a seat of it waits for your yes (the owner's ruling, 2026-10-09), and the sign-in names none — the door never picks an org for you. HTTP 409; nothing was minted (the passphrase was right). `orgs` lists the orgs you hold an active seat in ({slug, name}); a waiting seat is answered on your org list (GET /orgs) after a browser sign-in.Send the same sign-in with org: one of the slugs in `orgs` (or next naming a page of that org).index.js
client_ref_takenThis clientRef already filed DIFFERENT content (`filed` names that filing), on any door that takes one: a contribution, a grade, an answer, a wrap-up's card answer or a knowledge write (G2: a clientRef names its content; the same content again is a replay). Nothing was written.Send a new clientRef (or leave it out) to file it as new; send the same content to replay it.core.js knowledge/write.js preview.js
confirm_failedThe confirm's stream (a write tool with fileOnConfirm, sprint 19; publish or equip with its OnConfirm flag, 7.5b) could not finish: a database call failed while it waited or filed. Nothing more was filed by the stream; what landed before is in the preview's receipt.Send the same call again without fileOnConfirm: a retry files only what did not land.confirm.js
confirm_not_opennot-foundA client's answer to a confirm named no open confirm of the caller's: another person's elicitation, another session's, a wrong id, an answer after the window (50 s), a second answer, a preview already filed, or (7.5b) a retry naming another tool's confirm (sprint 19: another write tool's too) or a changed call (the same answer for each, so an id grants nothing). HTTP 400; nothing was recorded or filed.Nothing to retry: call the write tool again with fileOnConfirm for a new confirm, or without it once the person said yes.confirm.js mcp.js
content_requiredsave_file was sent no content. Nothing was saved.Retry with content (the document's text or its HTML) and a title.mcp.js

cross_site_resetPOST /account/reset flagged as arriving from a different site than this door, the same guard as POST /login's (sprint 21, 21.4a). Refused before the body is read: nothing written.Set the passphrase from the link's own page (GET /account/reset/<token>).index.js

d1_quotaCloudflare D1's daily free-tier row-read budget is exhausted for this worker — every authenticated call fails until it resets at 00:00 UTC (see `retryAfterMinutes`). email_not_asciiPOST /signup (and Control's add-person) refused an email holding a letter outside plain ASCII (sprint 7's review, A5): an account's email has one spelling, and SQLite's lower() folds ASCII letters only.
