email_unverifiedPOST /login (a script) for an email that holds no account yet, with the passphrase of its newest unverified join (sprint 21, 21.4a: the account flow): the email was never verified, so no account exists and nothing is signed in.Open the verification link the join's email carries (POST /account/resend {email} sends a new one), type the passphrase there, then sign in.index.js
emptyThe content/body sent (e.g. to save_file) was empty — zero bytes.Retry with real content.core.js
eval_mark_refusednot-allowedThe eval mark (a test run's own row: hidden from every real screen, removed by Control's clean-eval) was sent on a write to a real project by a person who is not a test seat. Nothing was filed.Leave eval out to file it for real, or file the test on an eval project (create_project {eval: true}) or as a test seat.core.js
for_requiredbrief (GET /brief) was sent no `for`: a hat or a ref. Nothing was read.Retry with for: a hat (management, engineering, organization, gtm, finance, partner, quality) or a ref (goal/<id>, q/<qid>, check/<id>, a node id, T-YYYYMMDD-NNN).extract.js
forbiddennot-allowedThe caller authenticated, but may not read/write this specific resource (a role's brief it can't read, a private artifact it doesn't own). Or, inside a preview then save_knowledge invalid_ops, a non-owner's op on a doc, a card or a card kind their role may not read, or on a card of such a kind.Do not retry unchanged — use a credential that holds the resource, or ask its owner.knowledge/schema.js
goal_cycleA knowledge batch would make a goal its own ancestor. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Point the goal's parent at a goal outside its own branch, then send the batch again.knowledge/schema.js
goal_rootsA knowledge batch would leave the project's goal tree with more than one root (a goal with no parent), or none. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Give every goal but the one root a parent, then send the batch again.knowledge/schema.js
google_join_expiredPOST /request-access with google=1 (sprint 21, 21.4c: the form Google filled in) when this browser holds no live Google identity for it: the join ticket was used, is past its 30 minutes, or was made in another browser. HTTP 410; nothing written.Continue with Google again (GET /auth/google/start?intent=join), or join with your email and a passphrase (POST /request-access without google).index.js
group_requiredsave_file needs a real `group` (which system-part this belongs to) — 'ungrouped' is refused outright by the schema.Retry with a real group name.core.js mcp.js
has_childrenA knowledge remove names a goal that still has child goals the batch does not remove. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Remove the children in the same batch, or give them another parent first.knowledge/schema.js
id_requiredThe call needs an `id` (or, for the pack door, `kind`+`id`) and none was sent.Retry with the id.broadcast.js build.js impact.js pickup.js
incomplete_itemPOST /broadcast/publish named a draft that is not complete (its grade is incomplete: what, why, touches naming one of skill, agent or workflow, gapRefs ["item/<slug>"] and a source link as proof). Nothing was filed.File the draft again with every field (FILING_ITEM_CALL), then publish the new one.broadcast.js
insufficient_scopenot-allowedThis MCP connection was granted read-only access (mcp:read); the tool called needs mcp:write.Reconnect with mcp:write, or ask whoever granted the connection to widen its scope — do not retry unchanged.mcp.js
invalid_accountnot-authenticatedPOST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): the email and the ACCOUNT passphrase do not prove an account. ONE answer for every case: no account for the email, an account with no passphrase yet, a wrong one, or a seat's own secret (a key an org's admin minted or set never creates an org). Nothing was written but the attempt, which counts in the account's lockout with the sign-in's failures.Use the passphrase you chose at sign-up (POST /signup with the operator's code); an account with none gets one there.orgs.js
invalid_invitenot-authenticatedPOST /signup with an org's invite link (sprint 12, 12.3): the link does not open a sign-up. ONE answer for every case: no such open link, already used, expired (7 days), replaced by a newer link for the same seat, or its seat was removed, reissued (a new key or passphrase set by the admin) or is waiting for its holder's yes. Nothing was written, not even an attempt.Ask the admin who invited you for a new link (Control: the person's row, New invite link).invite.js
invalid_linkPOST /account/verify or POST /account/reset with a link that opens nothing (sprint 21, 21.4a): expired (a verification works 24 hours, a reset 30 minutes), used already, never sent, or (a verification) a verified request of that email stands. ONE answer for every case; nothing written.Ask for a new link: POST /account/resend {email} (a verification) or POST /account/forgot {email} (a reset).index.js
invalid_loginnot-authenticatedThe email/password pair sent to POST /login didn't match a live account.Retry with the correct credentials — this is not a transient failure.index.js
invalid_opsAt least one knowledge item broke a rule, so NOTHING in the batch was written; `errors` lists each one as { index, kind, id, error, note } (the first 100; `count` is all of them).Fix every op named, then send the whole batch again (the same clientRef is fine: nothing was filed under it).knowledge/write.js
invalid_signupnot-authenticatedPOST /signup (sprint 7, 7.2): the email and code do not open a sign-up. ONE answer for every case: the email was never allowed by the operator, or the code is wrong, already used, expired, revoked, or was given for another email. Nothing was written but the attempt, which counts in the account's lockout with the sign-in's failures.Check the email and the code against the email that brought the code (sharingu sends it when a place opens); a lost, used or expired code is replaced only by the operator.index.js
invalid_tokennot-authenticatedAn OAuth access token the provider still holds, whose person the door refuses: their key or passphrase changed after the grant (G2 M1), or they were removed; or a grant made before connections carried their credentials' stamp (before G2: sprint 7, 7.5b — it could never be checked, so it ends; its error_description says so). Nothing was read or written.Connect the app again (the OAuth sign-in) — do not retry the same token.mcp.js
items_requiredA preview's or a write tool's body carried no items array (or an empty one, or over 200 for a write tool).Retry with at least one item.preview.js
kind_and_id_requiredThe pack door call needs both `kind` and `id`, and at least one was missing.Retry with both.
missing_artifactA knowledge image render names an artifact that does not exist or that you may not use (not one you banked, not public; the owner may use any). The two read the same, so an id is never confirmed to someone who cannot read it. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Bank the picture yourself (save_file, or POST /artifact with its image content type: png, jpeg or webp; an SVG is refused, file a wireframe instead) and send that id as data.artifact. The artifact must be your own or a public one.knowledge/write.js
missing_cardA knowledge card names in its refs a card that this project does not hold, or one the writer may not read, at the end of the batch (sprint 4, F1). Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops); the note and `near` name up to three of the project's own cards close to each missed ref.Send refs as cards of this project, card/<kind>/<id> (read kind card lists them), or file that card in the same batch.knowledge/schema.js
missing_fieldA knowledge upsert creates a new item without one of its kind's required fields (a goal's title, a question's question, a check's title, a card's name, a node's type and name, a doc's body, the aim, the template). Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Send the field the note names, then the whole batch again.knowledge/schema.js
missing_nodeA knowledge edge names a node that is not in the project at the end of the batch, or a render names a screen that is not a node of type screen there. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).File the node first (kind node; a render's screen as type screen), in the same batch or before.knowledge/schema.js
missing_parentA knowledge goal names a parent that is not a goal of the project at the end of the batch. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Send an existing goal's id as parent (read kind goal lists them), or file that parent in the same batch.knowledge/schema.js
missing_styleA knowledge render names a style that is not in the project at the end of the batch. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).File the style first (kind style, {id, css}), in the same batch or before, or leave style out.knowledge/schema.js
next_doneThis contribution's next action is done already (the answer's done says when and by whom: a person's pick_up done, or a later contribution naming it as parent). Nothing changed.Do not retry: file a new contribution with its own next action if more is owed.pickup.js
next_takennot-allowedSomeone else picked up this contribution's next action first; the answer's pickedUp names who and when. The first pick-up holds. Nothing changed.Do not retry unchanged: ask the person who holds it, or wait until they mark it done or release it. The contribution itself stays open to anyone.pickup.js
no_choiceA knowledge question is ruled (not open) and has options, yet names no choice (an option index or letter) and carries no label. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Send choice as the option's index (0 = A) or letter, or a label saying what was ruled.knowledge/schema.js
no_next_actionpick_up was sent a contribution that names no next action (its next {what, who?, by?}), so there is nothing to take. Nothing changed.Read the contribution; a next action is filed with it (next {what, who?, by?}), or file a new contribution with one.pickup.js
no_ownernot-allowedThe report backfill found no active owner to hold the reports it banks. Nothing was banked.Restore an active owner on /control, then run POST /backfill again.core.js
no_seat_herenot-allowedPOST /login: the email and password are right, but that account holds no seat in the org this address serves (sprint 7: one account per email, a seat per org). Nothing was signed in, and never a seat of another org. Also (sprint 7's review, A1) when your account's only seats WAIT for your yes (an org's admin added you while your account stood elsewhere): a JSON sign-in mints nothing until you accept them on your org list.Ask this org's admin to add you, or sign in at the address of the org your seat is in.index.js
no_sessionThere is no session token on this request to act on (nothing to sign out, or nothing changed).Nothing to retry — this caller was already signed out or had nothing to change.index.js
not_filedThe round filing did not reach the ledger and returned no reason of its own (a store hiccup, not the caller's input).Retry once; if it repeats, report it with the time.decisions.js
not_foundnot-foundThe door authenticated the caller fine, but the id/ref/key asked for does not exist, or isn't visible to this caller.Check the id for a typo; do not retry the same call unchanged.build.js core.js decisions.js docread.js extract.js impact.js index.js knowledge/screens.js knowledge/store.js mcp.js pickup.js
not_openThe question is already ruled (decided, provisional, superseded or moot), so it takes no answer. Nothing was filed.Do not retry unchanged: read the ruling with `decisions` and its qid; to argue with it, file a counter as the card's counterCall says.decisions.js knowledge/decisions.js
not_picked_uppick_up release was sent for a next action nobody holds. Nothing changed.Nothing to release; pick it up instead if it is yours to take.pickup.js
not_readyA write tool named a preview whose items of its operation are not all ready (verdict needs or refused), and the call did not ask for only "ready". Nothing was filed; notReady lists each such item's index and verdict.Fix those items and preview again, or call the tool again with only: "ready" to file the ready ones and leave the rest.preview.js
not_seatednot-allowedPOST /broadcast/equip named a project the caller holds no seat on (the owner may equip into any active project), or POST /broadcast/publish was pressed by a person seated nowhere in the org. Nothing was filed.Equip into a project you are seated on, or ask a person seated on that project (or the owner) to press it.broadcast.js
not_yoursnot-allowedPOST /broadcast/publish named a draft (kind item) that another person filed. Only a draft's own author publishes it. Nothing was filed. POST /orgs/seat (sprint 7's review, A1): the seat named is not one of YOUR account's seats waiting for your yes (another account's, one no longer waiting, or the request is not your own ACCOUNT session): HTTP 404, nothing changed, the same answer for every case.Publish one of your own drafts (GET /broadcast lists them under mine), or file your own with FILING_ITEM_CALL. For a seat: answer it from your org list (GET /orgs), signed in with your account's passphrase.accounts.js broadcast.js
nothing_to_filesprint 19: a write tool named a preview that holds no item of its operation (parts names each tool the preview's items are filed with). Nothing was filed.Call the tool the parts name, with its items.preview.js
only_ownernot-allowedPOST /orgs/seat with answer decline (2026-10-15, THE FIRST PASSPHRASE WAITS): the waiting seat is its org's only real owner, so declining it would leave the org with no active owner. HTTP 409, nothing changed: the seat still waits.Accept the seat from your org list (GET /orgs), or leave it waiting.accounts.js
open_has_choiceA knowledge question is open yet carries a choice. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Send choice null, or (the owner) rule it with status decided.knowledge/schema.js
ops_requiredThe knowledge write behind file carried no items, or an empty list. Nothing was written.Send ops: a list of 1 to 200 {kind, op, data}.knowledge/write.js
option_requiredAn answer to a published question is one of its options, chosen, never typed text (QBDD22130): the call carried free text (answer, a legacy item, an a_*/x_* field) or no integer option. Nothing was filed.Retry with qid and option, the index of one of the question's published options (0 for A, 1 for B, 2 for C); `decisions` lists them.decisions.js
org_by_invitenot-allowedPOST /orgs (sprint 12, 12.3): the account's passphrase was set by an org's invite link, so it proves only what that org's admin could hand over: it creates no org during the beta (the orgs join by the waitlist, the owner approving each). Nothing written but the proof's attempt.Ask the sharingu operator for a sign-up code: it confirms your email (POST /signup resets the passphrase and lifts the mark), then create your org.orgs.js
org_limitnot-allowedPOST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): this account has already created its org. During the beta an account creates ONE org (the free tier, docs/plan/PLATFORM.md §4 sprint 8), and may be a member of any number. Nothing written.Use the org you created, or ask an org's admin to add you; a second org of your own is raised by hand on request.orgs.js
org_name_reservednot-allowedPOST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): the address (slug) is a name the platform uses: the first segment of one of the door's routes (GET /capabilities lists them) or one of its fixed words (src/orgnames.js). Checked before anything is read; nothing written.Choose another address for the org.orgs.js
org_name_takenPOST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): another org holds that address (asked only after the account is proven). Nothing written.Choose another address for the org.orgs.js
org_suspendednot-allowedThe operator has suspended this org (sprint 8, 8.5: tools/operator.mjs suspend; the one key `suspended` in its org row's settings). Every door answers the org's own people this one 403 — its pages, its MCP calls, its REST calls and a sign-in's landing in it — and nothing is routed, counted or written. Nothing of the org was deleted: when the operator lifts the suspension (unsuspend) every read and write answers as before. It takes hold within a minute (the org row is cached a minute per isolate); lifting it is answered at once (a suspended row is read fresh before each 403). Anyone else meets what they always met (another org's credential: the one not-here answer).Do not retry: ask the operator, who suspends and lifts an org by hand during the beta.
org_unreachablenot-allowedA call named an org (orgSlug, or ?orgSlug= on a brain:// resource) this connection does not act in: a seat's credential (a bearer key, a seat grant, a session) acts only in its own seat's org; an account grant only in the orgs its account holds an active seat in; and a JSON-RPC batch acts in one org (its FIRST call's: the current org when that call names none). An account grant whose own org no longer holds its seat names its org on every call: one that names none is refused, never acting in another org by default (sprint 7's review). The answer is the same whether the org named exists or not. Nothing was read or changed. `orgs` lists the orgs this connection may name.Retry with one of the slugs in `orgs`, or leave orgSlug out to act in the current org; for a batch, send the call for another org on its own. To act in another org you belong to from a seat's connection, connect again by signing in with your account's passphrase.mcp.js
org_waitingPOST /orgs by an account whose own passphrase is right but whose email holds neither a used operator's code nor an approved request (sprint 21, 21.4a): a verified person still in line. The beta's orgs stay on the waitlist; nothing made but the proof's attempt.Wait for the approval (the person's status: GET /account; the operator's allow --request sends "You're in"), then create the org.orgs.js
owner_onlynot-allowedThis door/tool is owner-role only, and the caller isn't the org's owner. Or, inside a preview then save_knowledge invalid_ops, a member's op on a question's ruling: a status other than open, a choice, label, rationale, decidedBy, decidedAt or supersededBy, or an edit or remove of a ruled question; a non-owner writing a role's brief doc capsules/<role>.md or start-here.md; or a non-owner setting or changing roleVisibility.Do not retry unchanged — use the owner's own credential, or ask the owner to do this.index.js knowledge/decisions.js knowledge/schema.js knowledge/versions.js mcp.js versionsview.js
partner_refusednot-allowedpublish, equip or regrade (the MCP tools, or their REST twins POST /broadcast/publish, POST /broadcast/equip and POST /regrade), or a restore of a screen's take (a render upsert naming a take's hash on preview then save_knowledge, inside invalid_ops; POST /render/restore), was called by a Partner: the role CLASS (src/hats.js roleClassOf: people.role partner, or a typed outside label such as external-* or vendor). An outside collaborator works on the projects they are seated on and never publishes to the org's shelf, equips into a project, regrades its checks or restores a screen's previous take. Nothing was read or filed.Ask a member of the org to publish the draft, equip the item or regrade the checks or restore the take, or ask the admin to make you a member on Control.broadcast.js knowledge/schema.js knowledge/screens.js regrade.js
path_requireddoc (GET /doc/:path) was called without a path. Nothing was read.Send path: one of the docs `read` lists; start-here.md is the place to start.docread.js
plan_limitThe org is at a limit of its plan (sprint 8, docs/plan/PLATFORM.md §4: the ruled free and team numbers), and this WRITE would take it past: `limit` names which (people: seats active or waiting for their holder's yes; projects: active projects; items_month: ledger rows filed this UTC month — contributions, knowledge writes, grades; calls_day: MCP tools/calls and REST writes this UTC day; burst_minute: the same calls this minute; storage_bytes: stored files and screen pictures, each body once — src/plans.js STORAGE_USED_SQL, the one definition the check and the shown plan read; checked by a file upload and, since 8.5, by a knowledge write's new render or style bodies before any is stored), `used` and `allowed` the org's own numbers, `plan` the plan whose limits applied (an org whose plan names none reads free's), `adding` what a batch or a file would add, `retryAfter` the seconds until a calls window starts again. Nothing was written. Reads are never refused. A call refused at the door is HTTP 429 with Retry-After; a write past 80% of a limit lands and its answer carries planWarning {limit, used, allowed, plan, note} (a REST write also the x-sharingu-plan-warning header).For burst_minute or calls_day: wait retryAfter seconds, then send the same call. For any other limit: do not retry unchanged — free room (archive a project, remove a seat or a file) or ask the operator, who raises an org's limits by hand during the beta.
preview_changedA write tool was sent items whose digest (sha256 of the items as canonical JSON) differs from the preview's items of its operation, in their order: what would be filed is not what the person saw (or the preview was made before the split, sprint 19). Nothing was filed; items names the preview's items of that operation.Send the preview's items of that operation as previewed, or preview again, then file with the new previewId.preview.js
preview_expiredA write tool named a preview older than an hour, and nothing of its part had been filed. Nothing was filed.Preview the items again, then file with the new previewId.preview.js
preview_filedA write tool named a preview whose part of that operation was already filed; nothing was filed again. The answer carries that part's first receipt (what each item became).Nothing: read the receipt. File the preview's other parts with their own tools, or preview again to file something new.mcp.js preview.js
preview_id_requiredfile was sent no previewId of the form preview answers (P- and 16 hex). Nothing was filed.Send previewId: the id preview answered, and the items of the tool's operation, as previewed.preview.js
preview_not_foundnot-foundA write tool (file_contribution, save_knowledge, remove_knowledge) named a preview that is not the caller's own: none with that id, or another person's (the same answer either way, so an id grants nothing). GET /preview/:id answers its usual 404 for the same reasons. Nothing was filed.Preview the items again (preview) and file with the id it answers.preview.js
project_forbiddennot-allowedThe `project` named isn't one the caller may use: not one of their own seats (the owner: not an ACTIVE project) — on a write, or (U-MCP, projectScope) on a project-scoped READ at any door: an MCP tool's `project`, a GET twin's ?project= (403) or a brain:// resource's ?project= (-32003); or (U-MCP-tail-b) a non-string `project` (an object, array, number or boolean — `project` is one project key, a string); or an answer naming another project than its call (respond / round: one project per answer call). Nothing was read or filed. `seats` lists the allowed projects. Or (the knowledge door) a write to a project the caller holds no seat on, even the one project of a single-project org the door would otherwise stamp them into.Retry with one of the seats listed (the refusal's `note` and `example` name them), or ask for a seat on the project named.activity.js core.js decisions.js index.js knowledge/write.js mcp.js preview.js project.js
project_requiredThis caller holds more than one seat, so the write needs an explicit `project` to stamp — the server refuses to guess; or POST /broadcast/equip named no project and the request has none of its own; or (U-MCP-tail-b D6) submit_grade has no project to count against (a caller seated nowhere in a multi-project org) or its filing would be stamped into another project than the pack it reads — nothing is filed. Or preview / read resolved no project (a caller holding more than one seat with none active, or the owner seated nowhere in a multi-project org): nothing is written or read.Retry with `project` set to one of the seats listed — the refusal's `note` names them and its `example` carries one ready to send (for an equip: the project to equip into).broadcast.js core.js extract.js impact.js knowledge/decisions.js knowledge/grades.js knowledge/screens.js knowledge/store.js knowledge/versions.js knowledge/write.js preview.js regrade.js
q_requiredsearch (or GET /search) carried no search words (`q`; search counts words of two letters and up). Nothing was read.Retry with `q`.extract.js
question_requiredThe `ask` call carried no `question` — nothing to ask.Retry with `question`: what you want to ask the owner.ask.js
read_only_credentialnot-allowedThe credential used (e.g. a boot link / read-only key) can read but not write.Do not retry unchanged — use the full write-capable credential.broadcast.js confirm.js index.js knowledge/decisions.js mcp.js preview.js regrade.js
ref_requiredThe call needs a canonical `ref` (screen:NNN · c/<id> · q/<id> · mind/<area>) and none was sent; `read` (GET /read) was sent neither a ref nor a kind; or regrade (POST /regrade) was sent none of flow, node or checks.Retry with `ref` (regrade: flow, node or checks).extract.js regrade.js
ref_too_longThe `ref` sent is over the 80-character limit (see `max`).Retry with a shorter ref.core.js
refs_requiredimpact was sent neither a contribution id nor any ref it can read. Nothing was read.Send contribution: an id (T-YYYYMMDD-NNN), or refs: the ids you are about to change (screen:<id>, door:<method>:<path>, goal/<id>, q/<qid>, check/<id>).impact.js
release_forbiddennot-allowedOnly the person holding a next action, the contribution's contributor or the owner releases it. Nothing changed.Ask the person holding it (the answer's pickedUp names them) or the owner.pickup.js
reserved_kindnot-allowedA filing with kind publish, equip or knowledge reached file_contribution (a contribution item). Publish and equip are written only by a person's press on Broadcast, knowledge only by the knowledge write door (one row per save_knowledge or remove_knowledge call). Nothing was filed (a batch files none of its items).Do not retry with that kind: file a draft as kind item (FILING_ITEM_CALL) and let its author press Publish, or the people seated on a project press Equip, on Broadcast; write knowledge with preview then save_knowledge (POST /preview/save-knowledge).core.js
search_unavailablesearch (GET /search) found no full-text index on this org: migrate-056 is not applied yet. Nothing was read.Use `read` with a kind to list items meanwhile; the admin applies migrate-056.extract.js
session_requirednot-allowedA client's answer to a confirm came without the Mcp-Session-Id header the initialize answer gave; a confirm is bound to the session that asked. HTTP 400; nothing recorded.Send the answer with the session id initialize answered (Mcp-Session-Id).confirm.js
slug_requiredequip (or POST /broadcast/equip) was sent no slug: the item to equip, a slug on the shelf or preset:<slug> for a starter item. Nothing was read or filed.Retry with slug and v: `broadcast` lists the shelf and the starter items, each with its slug and version.broadcast.js
slug_takennot-allowedPOST /broadcast/publish named a draft whose item/<slug> another person published first; a slug belongs to its first publisher. Nothing was filed.File the draft again under another slug, then publish that one.broadcast.js
summary_requiredwrap_up needs a `summary` and none was sent.Retry with `summary`.handoff.js mcp.js
title_requiredThe call needs a `title` and none was sent.Retry with `title`.knowledge/versions.js openitems.js
too_few_optionsA knowledge question would end the batch open with fewer than 2 options, or ruled with exactly one. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Send data.options with 2 or more [{what, tradeoff}] (a ruling may carry none).knowledge/schema.js
too_largeThe content sent is over this door's byte limit (see `maxBytes`); on preview then save_knowledge (inside invalid_ops), a render's or a style's body over its limit (html 200 KB, css 200 KB, a wireframe 50 KB, an image 1 MB), a call whose carried bodies (html, css, wireframes) together pass 256 KB, or whose image renders' pictures together pass 1 MB — the error's index names the op.Retry with smaller content, or split it (a call's bodies: send the named op and the ones after it in another call).core.js knowledge/schema.js knowledge/write.js mcp.js render.js
too_many_attemptsThis account has failed sign-in too many times; a per-account cooldown is active (see `retryAfterMinutes`).Wait the stated cooldown before retrying — retrying sooner will not succeed.index.js orgs.js
too_many_attempts_ipThis IP has failed sign-in too many times; a per-IP cooldown is active (see `retryAfterSeconds`).Wait the stated cooldown before retrying.index.js
too_many_itemsA preview carried more than 200 items, or regrade (POST /regrade) named more than 60 checks (see `max`/`got`).Split into previews of 200 or fewer, or regrades of 60 checks or fewer.preview.js regrade.js
too_many_opsA preview or file carried more than 200 items (see `max`/`got`). Nothing was written.Split the batch into calls of 200 ops or fewer.knowledge/write.js
transcript_rejectedThe privacy door (ADR-016 d) refused this call because it appears to carry a raw conversation transcript.Do not retry unchanged — strip the transcript content and resend just the real payload.handoff.js index.js mcp.js
unauthorizednot-authenticatedThe bearer token sent didn't resolve to a person (missing, malformed, expired, or revoked).Send a valid Authorization: Bearer <token> and retry.broadcast.js index.js knowledge/screens.js regrade.js
unimplementedThe tool name called isn't wired to a handler in callTool's switch — a registry/implementation mismatch, not a caller mistake.Do not retry unchanged — report it; this is an engine defect.mcp.js
unknown_briefbrief with no `for` (or GET /brief?role=) named a role whose brief (the doc capsules/<role>.md) the project does not hold, or one your role may not read: the two read the same (see `briefs`).Name one of `briefs` as role, or file the brief: preview then save_knowledge, a doc at capsules/<role>.md.docread.js
unknown_checknot-foundsubmit_grade (POST /grade) or regrade (POST /regrade, checks) named a checkId the project's check register (k_checks) does not carry. Nothing was filed or regraded.List the project's checks with read {kind: "check"} (brief {for: <a ref>} for one item's), then retry with one of their ids; file a new check as an item {kind: "check", op: "upsert", data} through preview, then save_knowledge.knowledge/grades.js regrade.js
unknown_fieldA knowledge upsert sent a field its kind does not have. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).Send only the fields the note lists (formats {kind} lists every kind's), then the whole batch again.knowledge/schema.js
unknown_goalnot-foundGET /goals/:ref (the goal tool, brain://goal/{ref}) named a goal id that is not in this workspace's goal tree: missing, mistyped, or another project's (the same answer either way, M-ADR-028). Nothing was read.Read GET /goals (the goals tool) and use one of its nodes[].id; do not retry the same ref unchanged.index.js mcp.js
unknown_itemnot-foundPOST /broadcast/publish named no filing of kind item by that id, or POST /broadcast/equip named a slug nothing on the shelf carries. Nothing was filed.Read GET /broadcast (the broadcast tool): mine lists your drafts' ids, the shelf the published slugs.broadcast.js index.js
unknown_kindThe kind named isn't one the door knows: a knowledge item, a read / GET /read kind or a formats / GET /formats kind outside aim · goal · question · check · card · card_kind · node · edge · gtm · doc · render · style (see `kinds`), or a pack kind this workspace's pack does not declare. For search, read and changes: a kind outside the list their answer names in `kinds`.Retry with one of the kinds listed.extract.js formats.js knowledge/schema.js knowledge/store.js
unknown_nodenot-foundGET /map/node (map {ref}, brain://map/node/{ref}) named a node the published map does not carry: an unknown screen, door, table, entity or gap, a goal not in the served goal tree, or a gap index past the last OPEN gap; or regrade (POST /regrade) named a flow or a node the project does not hold. Nothing was regraded.Read GET /map/node?gap=1 (walk.n is the open-gap count) or GET /canvas.json for the ids the map carries; do not retry the same ref unchanged.mapnode.js regrade.js
unknown_optionnot-foundThe option index is not one of the question's published options. Nothing was filed.Read the question (`decisions` with its qid, or GET /question/:qid) and retry with one of its option indexes.decisions.js knowledge/decisions.js
unknown_parentnot-foundThe `parent` named is not a filing in the caller's project: no such id, or a filing in a project the caller holds no seat on (the two read the same, so the refusal never says a row exists elsewhere). Nothing was filed; a batch naming one is refused whole.Name an existing filing of your project as parent (read / GET /build list what you can see), or counter a question with gapRefs ["q/<qid>"] instead; then retry.core.js
unknown_planenot-foundGET /map/:plane (map {plane}, brain://map/{plane}) named a plane this worker does not serve: the served planes are arch, data, api, mcp, flows and deps (System is GET /map itself).Read one of the planes the answer lists (planes), or GET /map for System; do not retry the same plane unchanged.mapplanes.js
unknown_projectA knowledge node names in ownedBy (its data.ownedBy, or a part of its architecture's diagram) a project key that is not an active project the writer may read (sprint 4, M3: a name check on the org's projects, the writer's seats or, for the owner, every active project). Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops); `projects` lists the keys the writer may name, never the project written.Send ownedBy as one of `projects`, or leave it out.knowledge/schema.js
unknown_qidnot-foundNo published question carries this qid (or nothing is published for this project). Nothing was filed.Check the qid against `decisions` (GET /decisions); do not retry the same call unchanged.decisions.js knowledge/decisions.js
unknown_rendernot-foundA render upsert that restores a take (data.hash, no body) names a hash this project's takes do not hold: never filed here, or another project's (the two read the same). On preview then save_knowledge it rides in invalid_ops (nothing was written); POST /render/restore answers it 404.Send the hash of one of this project's takes (map {ref: "screen:<id>"} lists a screen's last six, each with its hash), or send the frame's body instead.knowledge/write.js
unknown_responsenot-foundA JSON-RPC response POSTed to /mcp answers no request this door sent (the door sends only elicitation/create on a confirm's stream, with an id sg-confirm:<previewId>:<nonce>). HTTP 400; nothing recorded.Do not send responses except to the door's own elicitation/create request.confirm.js
unknown_shapenot-foundformats (or GET /formats) named a shape that is not a lane. The answer lists the shapes.Send shape as one of the listed lanes.formats.js
unknown_surfacenot-foundGET /map/screens (map {plane: "screens"}) named a surface the project's screens do not name. Nothing else was read.Send one of the surfaces the answer lists (a screen node names its surface in data.surface), or leave surface out for the first.knowledge/screens.js
unknown_tabchanges (GET /changes) was sent a tab outside home · build · gtm · goals · decisions · map · broadcast · control. Nothing was read.Retry with one of the tabs listed in `tabs`, or leave it out.extract.js
unknown_tablenot-foundGET /map/data?table=<name> (map {plane} {plane:'data', table}) named a table the project's model (D1) does not carry. The answer lists the tables it does.Pick one of the listed tables (tables); do not retry the same name unchanged.mapplanes.js
unknown_versionnot-foundGET /versions/:v, POST /versions/restore or the versions tools named a version (a number or a content key) this project's spine does not carry; or POST /broadcast/equip named a version of an item beyond its newest (v1 to vN, the n-th publish). Nothing was filed. Or `changes` (GET /changes) was sent since: v<N> for a version the project does not carry. Nothing was read.Read GET /versions (the versions tool) for the versions that exist, or GET /broadcast for an item's newest version, then retry with one of them.broadcast.js extract.js knowledge/versions.js versionsview.js
unreachableGET /preview/:id (JSON) could not read the preview right now (a D1 error other than the daily limit). Nothing was read or written.Try again shortly.index.js
unreadableThe served state itself is marked unreadable, or (UI-B2: GET /decisions, GET /question/:qid) the published pack names a decisions file that is missing or not a list — a data problem on sharingu's own side, not the caller's; or (UI-B7b: GET /map/node; UI-B8b: GET /map/:plane arch and data, map {plane}) the canvas asset could not be read from storage.Do not retry unchanged — report it; this needs the brain's own state (or its pack publish) checked.activity.js decisions.js extract.js index.js knowledge/decisions.js knowledge/screens.js mapnode.js mapplanes.js
unsupported_imageA stored image render's body is not a png, jpeg or webp (an SVG filed before SVG renders were refused): GET /render/:hash answers 410 and does not serve it.File the render again as a wireframe, or as a png, jpeg or webp picture.knowledge/screens.js
write_failedThe knowledge batch passed every rule but the database refused it (the message rides in the note); D1 applies the batch and its ledger row together, so in the usual case nothing was written.Read the kinds back before retrying; a retry with the same clientRef is safe (a write that did land answers replay).knowledge/versions.js knowledge/write.js
wrong_passphrasePOST /account/verify with a live link but a passphrase that is not the one the join chose (sprint 21, 21.4a): the mailbox alone does not verify a request, so a stranger's join for an address cannot be completed by its owner's click. The attempt counts in the email's lockout; the request stays unverified.Type the passphrase chosen when asking to join (8 failures in 15 minutes are 429 too_many_attempts).
wrong_toolsprint 19 (the split door): a write tool was sent an item of another operation (items names each, what it is and the tool that files it: file_contribution a contribution, save_knowledge a knowledge upsert, remove_knowledge a knowledge remove; submit_grade a grade, respond an answer), or preview was sent a grade or an answer (that item is refused, naming submit_grade or respond). Nothing was filed.Send each write tool only the preview's items of its own operation, as previewed; file a grade with submit_grade and an answer with respond.preview.js

Verify

How it is proven: the commands, the gate, the store's cases and the beta gate.

The commands

Source: AGENTS.md · The commands (from engine/)

sh tools/smoke.sh                     # per slice: a fresh local worker, MCP write -> read -> the tabs (cases in tools/smoke/)
sh tools/dev-local.sh up              # the local app with REAL data: every project imported through the MCP; prints the URL
node tools/ship/after-import.mjs <url> --creds <file>   # then sharingu's history and screen pictures, through preview -> file
node tools/audit/project-audit.mjs --url <url> --creds <file>   # every project's data, read through the door
node tools/page-budget.mjs            # per slice: D1 rows read per screen and per MCP read (local, real data)
node tools/live-walk.mjs              # gate line 1: an admin and a new member on a throwaway project (--live after a ship)
sh tools/gate-rehearsal.sh <url> --creds <file>   # the seven gate lines against a local org
sh gate.sh                            # sprint end: the gate, green by exit code
sh evals.sh                           # sprint end: the eval suite, on a fresh local org (--live after a ship)
sh sims.sh                            # sprint end: the sims, never beside another suite
sh tools/tabs-verify.sh               # sprint end: each seat signs in and walks every tab of the rail
sh tools/verify-live.sh               # after every ship with --live: our tools reach the org's door as themselves
sh tools/cf-budget.sh                 # before anything live: the Cloudflare budget guard (it reads the account's plan)
node tools/make-listing-docs.mjs --check   # the listing's docs page against the contract (gate); generate: no flag (the contract), or --url <worker> --creds <file>
node tools/make-reviewer-org.mjs --url <worker> --local <persist dir> --config <cfg>   # the stores' reviewer org (sprint 9; M4: --live --config wrangler.jsonc --confirm-live ryuklabs-agent-r; codes printed once)
node tools/listing-walk.mjs --url <worker> --codes <the refresh's codes file>   # listing/test-cases.md's eight cases, each as its account (smoke s51 walks the same code)
sh tools/ship-plan.sh ryuklabs        # read-only: this ship's order — migrations, preflights, checks, rollback (--no-import: no import hook)
sh tools/migrate.sh migrate-0NN.sql   # one migration on live, a Time Travel bookmark first
sh tools/ship.sh ryuklabs             # the ONE deploy command, resumable by its run record (SHIP_PREVIEW_HOOK: a step on the preview)
node tools/operator.mjs allow --email <e> --live --config wrangler.jsonc --confirm-live ryuklabs-agent-r   # the operator: a sign-up code (printed once), refused once the beta's 50 places are taken unless --beyond-cap (sprint 12); also list-orgs · set-plan · raise · suspend (sprint 8) · set-openai-challenge · clear-openai-challenge (sprint 11) · requests · allow --request <id> · decline --request <id> (sprint 21) · requests · allow --request <id> (sprint 21: the open requests in line; approve one, its code printed once)
node tools/org-undo.mjs plan --org <id> --live --config wrangler.jsonc --confirm-live ryuklabs-agent-r     # one org's export / restore / verify / delete

A contract change: edit contracts/door.declared.json or the registries in engine/src/index.js, then python3 engine/tools/make-door-contract.py.

The store's test cases

Source: listing/test-cases.md · whole

Five positive and three negative cases, each a numbered walk of what you ask your AI or do, and what you should see, against the reviewer org: an organization called "sharingu review" that holds the real sharingu project (sharingu's own goals, decisions, map and docs) and a small "Sample project", with seven accounts, one for each class of person in a real org. The operator builds it with node tools/make-reviewer-org.mjs (from engine/) and hands you each account's email and sign-in code; the code is your passphrase.

AccountRoleHatsSees
adminthe org's ownerManagement, Financeboth projects, every tool
membera membernoneboth projects
deva memberEngineeringboth projects
bda memberGo-to-market, Organizationboth projects
marketinga memberGo-to-marketboth projects
testera memberQualityboth projects
partneran outside partnerPartnerthe Sample project only

The Sample project also holds an authored walkthrough, the Pilot Shop (a made-up online shop): three apps with their screens and wireframes, its API, its database schema, its flows and the apps it connects on the Map, and one request's whole loop on the goal "Pilot Shop: a business buyer pays by invoice", each step filed by the account that does it: the bd account proposes it, the admin approves it, the dev picks it up and files it done, the tester grades its checks, and marketing announces it. Every account reads it on that goal's page; brief for a hat reads what that hat needs first.

The MCP address: https://agent.sharingu.xyz/mcp. Add it to your client as a remote MCP server: in Claude, Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector; in ChatGPT, installing the sharingu plugin connects this server, or by hand: Plugins (https://chatgpt.com/plugins), the plus button, Add custom MCP server with this address and OAuth, then "I understand and want to continue". The client opens sharingu's sign-in: enter the account's email and its code. No header and no key go in the client's configuration. The org in a browser: https://agent.sharingu.xyz/sharingu-review, signed in with the same email and code. The tools named below are listed with who may call them on the docs page, https://www.sharingu.xyz/mcp-tools.html.

Each walk is what the product's own suites prove; tools/listing-walk.mjs walks all eight, each as the account its heading names: on live after a refresh (--url <worker> --codes <the refresh's codes file>; it files P3's and P5's notes and P4's accepted goal, as a reviewer would) and, through smoke case s51, in every smoke run, on a fresh reviewer org built with the sample alone: there the sharingu project is empty, so P2's sharingu reads are walked as answering, not as its tree (the full world, ~18,130 rows written with the sample by the importer's measure of 2026-10-10, is the tool's local proof).

Positive cases

P1 · Connect and sign in — account: admin

  1. Add the MCP address to your client and sign in as the admin.
  2. Ask your AI: "Call sharingu's whoami." (the whoami tool) Expect: your name (Reviewer Admin), the role owner, the org "sharingu review", and the two projects your writes can land in, sharingu and the Sample project.

Also: a wrong credential is refused before any tool runs. A wrong code at the sign-in answers invalid_login and makes no session; an MCP call with a made-up bearer token (Authorization: Bearer not-a-real-key) answers HTTP 401 invalid_token.

P2 · Read the real sharingu project — account: member

  1. Sign in as the member (in a new chat, or a second client).
  2. Ask: "Show me the goals of the sharingu project" (the goals tool, project sharingu). Expect: sharingu's goal tree, each goal with its status and progress.
  3. Ask: "Search the sharingu project for preview" (the search tool). Expect: matching goals, questions, docs and map nodes, each with a link.
  4. Open the org in a browser as the member. Expect: Home, Decisions and the Map show the same project.

P3 · File a contribution through preview, then file_contribution — account: member

  1. Ask: "In the Sample project, file a note in the leader lane: what 'A reviewer's first note', why 'the store's test case'. Preview it first." Expect: the preview (the preview tool) shows the one item, "files at once", names the tool that files it, and says nothing is filed yet.
  2. Ask: "File it." Expect: the receipt (the file_contribution tool) with the contribution's id, T- and the date and a number, and its link.
  3. Ask: "Read that contribution." (the read tool) Expect: what you filed, by Reviewer Member, in the Sample project.
  4. In the browser, open Build. Expect: the note is in the list.

P4 · The confirm: nothing is filed until you say yes — account: admin

  1. Ask: "In the Sample project, add a goal 'A reviewer goal' under the goal 'Every contribution closes the loop', and file it only after I confirm." (the preview tool, then save_knowledge with its confirm) Expect: the preview shows the goal and files nothing; then either your client asks you to confirm, showing what would be filed, or (a client that shows no confirm prompt) sharingu answers that you were not asked and files nothing.
  2. Decline (or, where you were not asked, do not file). Expect: "The person declined: nothing was filed." where you were asked; nothing filed either way.
  3. Ask: "Read the goal 'A reviewer goal'." (the read tool) Expect: there is no such goal (not_found).
  4. Ask again and accept (or, where you were not asked, say "File it.": save_knowledge again, without the confirm). Expect: the goal is filed; it reads back under its parent, and the Goals tab shows it.

P5 · A partner works only where it is seated — account: partner

  1. Sign in as the partner.
  2. Ask: "Call whoami." (the whoami tool) Expect: the role partner and ONE project, the Sample project.
  3. Ask: "Show the Sample project's goals." (the goals tool) Expect: its goal tree.
  4. Ask: "In the Sample project, file a note in the leader lane: what 'A reviewer's first note', why 'the store's test case'. Preview it, then file it." (preview, then file_contribution, as in P3) Expect: a receipt with its T- id.

Negative cases

Each is a request your AI should not carry out: why, then the refusal or the safe fallback you should see.

N1 · Nothing is deleted through the AI — account: admin

Why: sharingu has no tool that deletes or archives a project; a project is the owner's to archive on Control, in the browser, and an archive is never a delete. remove_knowledge removes a project's knowledge items (a goal, a doc, a Map node), never the project itself, and only items a preview showed first.

  1. Ask: "Delete the Sample project and everything in it." Expect: your AI says it cannot: no sharingu tool deletes a project. Nothing changes: whoami still lists both projects, and the Sample project's goals still read. If it offers to remove the project's items one by one instead, that starts with a preview, which removes nothing; and a project is no item a preview can name (unknown_kind).

N2 · A partner cannot read a project it has no seat on — account: partner

Why: a partner was invited to the Sample project only; the rest of the org is not its to read.

  1. Ask: "Show the sharingu project's goals." Expect: refused with project_forbidden, naming the projects the partner holds (the Sample project only) and how to name one. No goal of sharingu is shown.

N3 · A member cannot call an owner's tool — account: member

Why: making a project is the org owner's decision; a member works in the projects it is seated on.

  1. Ask: "Create a project called Mine" (the create_project tool). Expect: refused with owner_only; no project is made (the admin's Control page lists only the two projects).

The beta gate

Source: docs/plan/BETA.md · whole

One page: what beta means, and the proof each line closed with. The slices are in SPRINTS.md; what happens next is HANDOFF.md's queue (the invites, then the platform road in PLATFORM.md).

What "beta" means (the gate — every line is checked on LIVE)

  1. A new member, end to end. Invited on Control → connects their Claude with the command Connect shows → gets or creates a project → hands Claude real input (a repo, docs, screenshots, a discussion) → sees the preview → files → every tab fills and the meter moves → answers one question → grades one check → files one change and sees its impact and the stale light → regrades. Walked by node tools/live-walk.mjs on a throwaway project AND once by hand.
  2. Our five projects are live (sharingu, ryuklabs, siru, saruspay, bunny), each with its screens atlas, and each meter matches what the data really holds (MCP.md §6).
  3. Three clients proven: Claude Code (the inline render and the confirm), Claude desktop or web (the card), and one tools-only client (Codex or ChatGPT) through the two-call fallback.
  4. Inside the budget: no screen or MCP read over 1,500 rows. On our account (Workers Paid) a day of the walk plus normal use is priced against the month's allowance; on a stranger's free account it stays under half of every daily limit. Proven on live 2026-10-05 (SPRINTS.md, S4-1): the day after the ship, with the walk, the grading run and the crons, cost 132 requests, about 1.46 million rows read and about 45,000 rows written — 0.1%, 29% and 45% of a free account's daily limits.
  5. Safe: one adversarial read of the auth and the render sandbox done and fixed; the backup includes the knowledge tables; a rollback command is written down for every ship.
  6. Honest docs: docs/INSTALL.md, Control · Connect and the built-in start-here name only the new tool names (measured by tools/names-check.mjs).
  7. A stranger can install it (owner, 2026-10-01: an outside beta team runs sharingu on its OWN Cloudflare account): a fresh org is minted on a second Cloudflare account from docs/INSTALL.md alone, its first run leads straight to "create a project and fill it", and the member path of line 1 passes there.

Not in the gate: the Claude plugin (PLATFORM.md sprint 9) and the store listings (MARKETPLACE.md). The release form and its licence were ruled at the close (below, item 6).

The rule for the rest of the road (owner, 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02)

Everything is built, tested and fine-tuned END TO END on the local app first, on real data. Nothing goes to Cloudflare until the local run of the gate is green. The old path is deleted before the ship (no dead code, no dead docs): done (D6a, and D6b with the names). The second video is recorded LAST of the local steps. Then ONE push: the migrations in order, the org's row written on live from its served tenant.json (tools/org-row.py, through tools/migrate.sh), one ship, the gate on live.

How each line closed (2026-10-05/06)

Sprints 1–4 are merged to main (the slices sprint by sprint: SPRINTS.md); live runs sprint 5 (shipped 2026-10-06, the record in HANDOFF.md). Sprint 4 closed the machine-provable gate lines: line 4 proven on live (below), line 5's adversarial read done and fixed (the sprint-4 review), line 5's restore rehearsed against a remote D1, line 6 measured by tools/names-check.mjs, and the Map built. The road after the ship, where each stands:

  1. The sprint-4 ship — DONE (2026-10-05, the owner's OK): the walk on live 13/13, verify-live 18/18.
  2. Line 1's hand walk — DONE: the scripted walk 13/13 on live; a real-browser member walk 10/10 (engine/.runs/hand-walk-s4/).
  3. Line 3, the three clients — CLOSED, done and approved by the owner (2026-10-05): the tools-only two calls on live (T-20261005-043); Claude Code through sharingu-live (the two-step filed T-20261005-045; the confirm's door side proven — Claude Code desktop declares elicitation and auto-declines without a card, so its users get the two-step until that client fixes it, the finding in HANDOFF.md); the card through the claude.ai custom connector over OAuth, signed in as the owner seat (whoami → rl-owner-0001, owner-class tools exposed).
  4. The second video — DONE (the final take ~/Desktop/sharingu-walkthrough-v2.mp4, 3:26).
  5. Line 7 — the stranger's install: CLOSED for beta (owner, 2026-10-05) by the local run from docs/INSTALL.md alone (a fresh clone, r-local.sh up, the first-run ritual, day0-verify 17/17); re-proven on the platform's first-run path (sprint 7, 7.6: r-local.sh up <name> --empty, the operator's code → sign-up → create the org, day0-verify 25 passed, 0 failed); the second-Cloudflare-account run happens with the first outside team's real install.
  6. The release form and its licence — RULED (owner MCQ 2026-10-05: collaborator invites + docs/BETA-NOTE.md, MIT as-is; public with the plugin). Left: the invites themselves — the one open item, the owner's; ruled 2026-10-06: they go out after sprint 7's hosted front door ships, none before.

Known risks, and the answer to each

RiskAnswer
A stranger's free account allows about 10 ms of CPU and 50 subrequests a request, which the local worker does not enforce (sanitising and hashing 50 real renders took about 12 ms on the Mini)the importer's --max-bytes ladder; the door's 256 KB body cap a call refuses clearly; the stranger's install is rehearsed on a second account
The card and the confirm need a streamed answer from the workerbuilt (D3) and proven by a selftest client; the three real clients are walked by hand at the gate; the two-call preview → file always works
One sprint with everything means one large reviewper-slice commits; the reviewer reads slice by slice
The Mini is sharedsuites only under load 8, one at a time

Rules this road has taught

  • A builder's "green" is a claim. The main session reruns the smoke, every selftest and the row budget, commits, then runs the gate.
  • A screenshot is not a signed-in user. A new kind of request (a frame, an image, a poll) is checked on the cookie-only path (tools/shots.mjs --cookie, or a real browser) before the commit.
  • Rows written are counted, not estimated. An import states its count from the local worker first.
  • A migration the code depends on goes live before the code.
  • A doc names only what exists; history is deleted, not annotated (tools/check-docs.py is a gate step).
  • New asks go into a step or after beta. Nothing new is added without removing something or moving the gate.

The ship recipe

Source: engine/CLAUDE.md · Ship; Long runs leave a trail; One database, every org

sh tools/ship-plan.sh ryuklabs [--no-import] prints this ship's order, read-only (--no-import: a ship with no import hook — the projects' data is not on the platform road). sh tools/cf-budget.sh, then sh tools/ship.sh ryuklabs — the ONE deploy command, resumable by its run record (engine/.runs/ship/, keyed by what ships; a rerun says what it reused): the gate by exit code; live's schema level and its org names checked against this code's reserved names (tools/check-org-names.mjs --slugs) BEFORE the upload; a version upload with no traffic, a smoke on the preview URL, the cross-org suite on the preview (tools/attack-xorg.mjs --url: two throwaway orgs restored, walked both ways, deleted — never org 1), the walk on the preview (tools/live-walk.mjs --preview, as the suites' org), 10%, 100%, and a rollback on any failed smoke. During the canary mix the OLD version's share enforces no sprint-8 limit (the migrations land before the code by design): brief, and over at 100%. Never a bare wrangler deploy on the live worker (only a second platform's first deploy is plain, inside tools/new-org.sh, ORG-SETUP.md). Undo: sh tools/ship.sh rollback [<version-id>] (it refuses while migrate-068's triggers stand: their down script first). The operator's tools run on the deployment's credentials, never through a seat: tools/operator.mjs (allow / list / revoke an email's sign-up code, remove-account; sprint 8: list-orgs with each org's plan and usage, set-plan, raise — a NAMED plan row, never free's or team's ruled numbers — and suspend / unsuspend, one reversible 403 at the org's resolve; sprint 11: set-openai-challenge / clear-openai-challenge, the platform's one OpenAI domain-verification token in the deployment's KV, answered at /.well-known/openai-apps-challenge by src/wellknown.js; sprint 12: allow counts the beta's 50 places — BETA_ORG_CAP (src/beta.js since sprint 21), the owner's one number: the outside orgs that stand plus the allowed emails with an open code and no org yet — and refuses past them unless --beyond-cap; list and list-orgs say the count at their head; the worker does not enforce it; sprint 21: requests lists the open (verified) requests for a place in line order, and allow --request <id> approves one — the same cap, then one guarded write and ONE "You're in" email through src/email.js sendMail (counted in the cap; --live by Cloudflare's REST send, --local into the local capture; --origin the links' start), no code; an approved request with no org holds a place; decline --request <id> declines an open one in one guarded write, no code; 21.4c: set-google-client --file <path> / clear-google-client, the platform's one Google OAuth client in the deployment's KV, read from a mode-600 file and never printed) and tools/org-undo.mjs (one org's export, restore, verify, delete). Credentials: set -a; . ~/.sharingu/env-sharingu.sh; set +a (a bare wrangler hangs on a login prompt).

Migrations are expand then contract (below) and applied one at a time with sh tools/migrate.sh <file> (a D1 Time Travel bookmark first), rehearsed first with sh tools/migrate-dryrun.sh ryuklabs-agent-r --from <NNN>. ship.sh never runs one.

Long runs leave a trail

  • A long run writes its record BEFORE it acts, so a restart resumes instead of re-paying: the preview attack's per-run orgs record under engine/.runs/ship-xorg/ (then --cleanup <run dir> finishes a killed run), org-undo.mjs's run record and refusing delete, tools/ship/r2-org-keys.mjs's state file (idempotent copy, delete only after a fresh complete verify), a builder's engine/.runs/<name>/PROGRESS.md, and docs/plan/HANDOFF.md at every stop.
  • The restart drill: read the newest run record under engine/.runs/, clean what it names, resume from HANDOFF.md's order. A milestone is only reused when its key still holds (the same uploaded version id; for ship.sh, the same SHIPPED content — engine/ and contracts/ as committed — so a HANDOFF edit mid-ship keeps the resume, and a reused gate still re-runs the docs gate) — never "step N was done". ship.sh's run record lies under engine/.runs/ship/; a rerun says what it reused.
  • Never edit a script a running ship is executing (or a tool it will spawn later in that run): the shell reads incrementally and node reads at spawn — land such changes between runs.

One database, every org

  • A migration is expand then contract, always: nothing renamed or dropped in the step that adds. Its header says whether it lands BEFORE or AFTER the code (migrate-067 before; migrate-068 and migrate-069 after).
  • Time Travel is a platform incident tool: it restores the WHOLE database, every org. One org's undo is the per-org restore, node tools/org-undo.mjs (plan, export, restore, verify, delete) on the deployment's credentials.
  • The canary reaches every org, so the preview runs the cross-org suite and the walk before any traffic moves.
  • A preview hook writes live data only for the org it was started for.
  • A migration's dry run uses a copy holding at least two orgs (migrate-dryrun.sh adds one to a copy of one).
  • One org never blocks the rest: the per-screen row budget (node tools/page-budget.mjs) and a rate limit per org (sprint 8's, docs/plan/PLATFORM.md §4).
  • Before the waitlist opens: the per-org restore rehearsed on live, the attack suite green on live, and the privacy page saying who can reach a hosted org's data.
  • The wall is in the gate: tools/check-scoped-data.py fails a statement or an R2 key outside src/data.js and src/storage.js; tools/attack-xorg.mjs walks every tool, resource and route as one org against another.

The traps

Source: docs/plan/HANDOFF.md · Traps a session must know

Ships

  • The cross-org suite on the preview runs 50 minutes to almost 3 hours with a QUIET log. A quiet log is not a stall: check the attack-xorg.mjs process's CPU time moves and it holds an ESTABLISHED socket; its progress is the preview version's request count (engine/.runs/repro-500/gql.sh <from> <to>, ~11,700 for a whole run). ship.sh prints "✓ live: <id> at 100% (the rollback target)" at its START: that is not the end.
  • A request to a VERSION PREVIEW URL is invisible to wrangler tail AND to Workers Logs; only the GraphQL analytics (workersInvocationsAdaptive by scriptVersion and status) see it. A 1101 the analytics never counted as an exception is the edge, not us.
  • runPreview fails on ANY 429 (counted as plan_limit): a route that spends the address's LOGIN_LIMIT budget must join attack-xorg's SKIP (or be paced), or the preview goes red while every local run stays green. For the same reason, never run sign-ins on live (a reviewer walk, a live walk) WHILE a ship's suite runs: they share the address's budget.
  • Never change the database's orgs (a delete, a restore) while a ship's suite runs: it compares every other org's rows.
  • A dirty tracked file under engine/ makes the run record non-resumable and tags the version -dirty: commit first.
  • gh pr merge can hit a "base modified" race: never chain a branch delete after it; check the state first.
  • A ship window crossing 03:00 or 15:00 UTC meets the cron's backup heartbeat (the suite excludes its exact shape; never widen that).
  • After the triggers deploy, this Mini's resolver may cache a negative answer for agent.sharingu.xyz for about two minutes (curl rc 6): test with a resolver override before calling it an outage.
  • The live walk needs a credentials FILE with an *_AGENT_R_OWNER_KEY= line, which env-sharingu.sh does not have. Make a throwaway one and delete it after: umask 077; f=~/.sharingu/tmp/walk-$$.env; printf 'RYUKLABS_AGENT_R_OWNER_KEY=%s\n' "$SHARINGU_RYUKLABS_ADMIN_KEY" > $f; node tools/live-walk.mjs --url https://agent.ryuklabs.io --creds $f --live --operator-config wrangler.jsonc --confirm-live ryuklabs-agent-r; rm -f $f. verify-live: if it SKIPs its authenticated checks on a transient Cloudflare read, run it again; 13/13 is not 28/28.
  • wrangler kv key delete takes the KEY FIRST (npx wrangler kv key delete "<key>" --namespace-id <id> --remote); a -- before the key makes it fail with rc 1 and delete nothing.

Accounts

  • ryuk@ryuklabs.io is the owner's REAL account: never remove-account it, never test a join with it. Test the join with a plus address on a mailbox you can read (ryuklabs.io is Google Workspace: ryuk+test@… lands in ryuk@'s inbox; the per-mailbox limit counts it as ryuk@).
  • remove-account refuses an account with an active seat or a standing org it founded: delete the org first (tools/org-undo.mjs export, then delete).

Email and Cloudflare

  • Cloudflare Email Routing takes ONE destination and ONE action per rule; a destination must be VERIFIED by its holder's click before forwarding reaches it.
  • The deployment's token reads and writes Email Routing but has NO DNS read and NO zone analytics: check records with dig +short <name> @1.1.1.1 (DoH lookups from this Mini time out at times; IPv4 to Cloudflare can take ~16 s a call while IPv6 takes ~1 s), and a delivery by sending a test to a mailbox you can read.
  • The binding sends from: {email, name}; Cloudflare's REST send takes {address, name} (tools/operator.mjs restBody).

Secrets and codes

  • Any tool that prints codes "once, on this terminal" prints them into the session's transcript: always redirect its stdout to a mode-600 file and count lines; never cat it. Never print a key, a code, a token or a person's email.

Local worlds

  • A STANDING local world (dev-local, a reviewer world) misses migrations a newer code expects: after a ship with a migration, apply it by hand (npx wrangler d1 execute <db> --local --config <its wrangler.local.jsonc> --persist-to <its persist> --file migrate-0NN.sql) before dev-local.sh up (a PLATFORM.md §3 row will automate it).

Videos and screens

  • Screenshots of a LOCAL worker under the public name (agent.sharingu.xyz) LEAK: map the name and refuse every other host (Chromium --host-resolver-rules=MAP agent.sharingu.xyz 127.0.0.1:<port>, MAP * ~NOTFOUND, wrangler --local-protocol https --upstream-protocol https), and send every request from inside the page (page.evaluate(fetch)), never Playwright's request context (it resolves with node's own DNS).
  • Claude can NEVER be granted computer-use control of Claude's own app: a Claude Desktop take is the owner's to record.
  • A macOS screen recording is variable-frame-rate: transcode to constant 25 fps with a keyframe every second BEFORE pinning any cut (ffmpeg -i in.mov -vf fps=25 -g 25 -keyint_min 25 out.mp4), then sweep EVERY half second of what is kept. This ffmpeg has no drawtext: captions are rendered as PNGs (engine/.runs/b12-videos/captions.mjs).
  • A filing through mcp-remote (Claude Desktop's config bridge) reads "from another client" (a PLATFORM.md §3 row).

The shell and the harness

  • The Bash tool's shell is zsh: an unquoted $VAR is not word-split, an unmatched glob is an error, there is no timeout command, and sh -c '…' holding rm trips the harness's safety check. Put multi-step scripts in a file.
  • Gate a heavy run on load INSIDE its own command ([ load -lt 8 ] || exit); printing uptime is not a check. bunny's simulator runs spike the load in waves: wait, never skip.

Gaps

Every open item, from the one list: missing flows, known issues, hardening and the owner's items.

Gaps and issues

Source: docs/plan/PLATFORM.md · §3 The residual ledger (THE one list of open items)

Every open item, from the one list. To pick one up: say so to the main session, take it in the current sprint's branch as a slice, and tick it out of docs/plan/PLATFORM.md §3 when its smoke is green.

Missing flows 20

How a dev closes one: A flow a hosted team product is expected to have. Close it as a vertical slice: the table, the MCP/REST write, the screen that reads it, a smoke case; an auth change gets an adversarial review before its PR.

Known issues 23

How a dev closes one: A fault found in a build or a review. Reproduce it in a selftest first, fix it, keep the selftest.

Hardening 17

How a dev closes one: The platform's pre-public hardening (rows marked S9). Measure first (page-budget, the cross-org suite), change, measure again; a schema change is its own expand-then-contract migration.

The owner's items 15

How a dev closes one: Only the owner can do or rule these. Bring them as an MCQ with the recommended option first; never act on them alone.

Decisions

What the owner ruled, the marketplace road and what only the owner prepares.

The owner's rulings

Source: docs/plan/HANDOFF.md · Ruled by the owner; The direction

Beta is green and the ryuklabs team uses live: keep live stable for real users. sharingu is a hosted platform (one worker and one database for every org) with a Claude plugin; the marketplace listings are the main aim now. Every change rides the same process: one sprint branch, vertical slices, one review and ONE ship at sprint end with the owner's OK. Clean all the way: no dead code, no dead docs; a finished brief is deleted.

Tests focused on the change's region2026-10-15

while building, the touched selftests and only the smoke cases a change touches; the full smoke and the gate once before the sprint's PR; the cross-org suite stays whole on every code ship (the wall's guard) but gets faster; no ship for a change to docs or the plugin alone. The tooling is sprint 22's first slice; until it lands, today's process stands (AGENTS.md).

Who holds an account2026-10-15

an account with a passphrase, a Google subject, an invite mark, or an active or pending seat is held: its join gets "you already have an account", never the beta line (ACCOUNT_HELD). A reset or Google's first link that sets an account's FIRST passphrase makes its active seats wait for the holder's yes (no role exempt; the operator's own sign-up code exempt); an org's only real owner cannot decline its waiting seat.

The join is told one way2026-10-15

request access, confirm the email, the operator's approval and its email, then create the org. The connector's suggested name is sharingu for every org; the front pages' top bar names the Walkthrough (the site's docs.html#walkthrough).

The operator2026-10-15

the operator page opens for an admin of org 1 only; there is no narrower role. Who operates the beta is the owner's grant.

The forms2026-10-15

submitted only after everything ships green; connector first (P1–P3 and the "from Claude" check), then the plugin; video 1 re-recorded after the forms.

Onboarding2026-10-13/14

the beta's 50 orgs, first come, first served, the owner approving each request; emails From hello@sharingu.xyz under the cap; Google sign-in; the team's alert to acie@ cc ryuk@; the data collected as the privacy page says (consents with their version, the source, the 90-day clearing).

The MCP is the only input; every write is previewed, then filed; the …

The MCP is the only input; every write is previewed, then filed; the word is "contribution".

Screens are optional for work that touches no screen; ids are checked …

Screens are optional for work that touches no screen; ids are checked against the project's own Map; proof is a stated result with its numbers, a command with its result, or a link — only narration is refused.

A plan or note feeds the goal it names and moves no code cell. Goals …

A plan or note feeds the goal it names and moves no code cell. Goals and GTM open on all time.

A new picture of a screen does not make its grades stale.

A new picture of a screen does not make its grades stale.

Anyone seated may publish their own draft to the shelf; a Partner may …

Anyone seated may publish their own draft to the shelf; a Partner may not.

The projects' data2026-10-02

ryuklabs' private data (client names with amounts, funding details) is stripped, on live too, and it holds no product model by design; siru's aim is its proposed mission, its tree's top the Thiruvallur pilot, its measure the pharmacies with doors open in that pilot; bunny's measure is the ask → TestFlight lead time per week; saruspay's the go-live checklist items done, of 61; sharingu's is activated organisations; Siru, FlowZo and Redacted/TOKEN2049 are approved claims with their boundaries. The projects' data is not on the platform road (2026-10-06).

PROPRIETARY2026-10-09

© Ryuk Labs, all rights reserved; the engine's repo stays private for good; the beta is hosted-only (docs/BETA-NOTE.md: no SLA, feedback asked); the plugin installs free from its own public distribution repo ryuk-labs/sharingu-plugin, the service is the priced product (prices at billing time).

The platform2026-10-06

one worker and one database for every org; the wall is org-carrying project keys; what happens in an org stays in the org (no staff seat in the app; only the deployment credentials reach the data); each org at agent.sharingu.xyz/<org>, the AI at the one /mcp; payment after the beta succeeds.

The suites' cut stands2026-10-03

the 80 cases plus the restored proofs.

Links, ids, invites and limits2026-10-06

a public file's link stays readable from any org and contribution ids stay numbered across the database; ONE revisit of both together before sign-up opens to everyone. The free tier: 1,500 items a month and 1,000 calls a day; raising by hand on request is the paid plan during the beta.

The beta-ops grant2026-10-06

for the beta the session drives ryuklabs org admin itself as the owner-class service seat agent-ops (attribution and approval_audit show Agent Ops, never the owner). The key is machine-local (SHARINGU_RYUKLABS_ADMIN_KEY in ~/.sharingu/env-sharingu.sh; the wrapper ~/.sharingu/rl-admin.sh). The surface: people, seats, open items, clean-eval through Control and the door, plus SQL for what Control lacks. Ships, schema migrations, money and other orgs still ask the owner. RETIRE AT THE BETA'S END: archive agent-ops on Control, drop the env line, remove the allow rules.

Frictionless start2026-10-10

the GTM filing skill files summaries and links only, never raw mail or DM text, each item previewed. A seventh hat, Quality, joins the six of 2026-10-01; the showcase world seats each class of an org.

Which AI filed it2026-10-11

each contribution stores one self-declared family word (claude, claude-code, chatgpt, codex, web, api, other), never the raw string; the privacy page says so.

The write door split2026-10-13

each write is its own tool, by what it does (file_contribution, save_knowledge, remove_knowledge); preview only shows and names the tool for each item; grades through submit_grade, answers through respond; every write is still previewed first.

The walkthrough2026-10-13

the videos are PUBLIC on the site's docs page, #walkthrough (one fixed URL: ChatGPT's demoRecordingURL); the OpenAI submission waits for the owner's ChatGPT recording to join that section.

The graders are destructive2026-10-12

submit_grade and regrade carry destructiveHint: true; a write that only adds stays non-destructive.

The one structural decision — ruled: hosted, one address (owner, 2026-10-06)

A directory listing points every user at ONE address. Until 2026-10-06 every org had its own worker and address and M3 was parked (MCQs 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-05). On 2026-10-06 the owner made sharingu a hosted platform: one worker and one database for every org, each org at agent.ryuklabs.io/<org>, the AI at the one /mcp there, joining by request and the operator's approval (sprint 21), payment after the beta succeeds. The design, the sprints and every open item: PLATFORM.md. The release ruled on 2026-10-05 stands: beta teams by GitHub collaborator invite with docs/BETA-NOTE.md. OVERTURNED 2026-10-09 by the owner: sharingu is PROPRIETARY (© Ryuk Labs) and the engine's repo stays PRIVATE for good — the plugin is distributed from its own small PUBLIC repo holding only the plugin folder (no engine code; synced from this repo). The plugin installs FREE; the SERVICE is the priced product (the platform's plans; prices at billing time). The beta is hosted-only.

History

Every sprint, newest first.

Sprint by sprint, newest first

Source: docs/plan/SPRINTS.md · every ## Sprint

A sprint is one branch. A slice is one commit (or a few) that goes: table → MCP/REST write → the screen that reads it. A slice is done when sh engine/tools/smoke.sh is green and its smoke case is in that script. Tick [x] with the commit sha. The full suites, the one review, the PR and the ship happen once, at sprint end.

Design rules for every slice:

  • Pages read D1 through engine/src/knowledge/ and engine/src/hotsql.js; a page never reads R2 for knowledge.
  • A page is one read function (its JSON twin and its MCP read tool answer from the same call) and one renderer.
  • An empty state is a short phrase and at most one button (LOOK.md, the revision); the call that fills it is listed on What is missing, never printed on the page.
  • When a slice replaces a page, delete the old module and its old text pins in the same slice.
  • One statement per screen region, indexed on (project, …). Run node tools/page-budget.mjs after every slice: a load over 1,500 rows read is flagged (a stranger's org may run on the free tier).
  • A migration takes the next free number at integration time; its header states its order against the code.

The whole record

The scope the owner ruled: a short splash (the owl, under 1.5 s, first visit only, skippable, off under reduced motion); request access with a profile (name, work email, company, role, team size; optional website, LinkedIn, X, GitHub, the AI tools used, one line of use case), which prefills the org at sign-up; a "you're in line" page with the person's place and the live beta count (N of 50, read from D1, never invented), what comes next and the walkthrough while they wait; "see the walkthrough" as a showcase call to action; the platform's sign-in and sign-up pages in the website's look; Google sign-in (sign-up, sign-in and the connect page; matched by email; still behind the operator's approval; the reviewer accounts keep their passphrase; needs the owner's Google Cloud OAuth client — none exists in sharingu today).

The shape the owner ruled (the second MCQ, 2026-10-13): request access is a worker page writing D1 (the site's waitlist button links to it; its Telegram-only form retires); an unsigned visitor at / gets a small showcase (the splash once, U-chan, one line, "See the walkthrough", "Request access", "Sign in"), replacing / → /login; a request is approved by operator allow --request <id> (the cap checked, the code printed once, the org prefilled from the profile), and the worker reads the SAME beta count for "N of 50" (the cap and its SQL move from tools/operator.mjs into src/, one source); Google sign-in lands last in this sprint, once the owner's OAuth client exists. Each slice: the table, the write, the screen, a smoke case; the old checks that pinned the replaced pages' text are deleted, not re-pinned.
